title: Information Security Compliance Intern
description: Sprinto is an Autonomous Trust Platform that centralizes trust requirements across security frameworks, vendors, and customers. Sprinto autonomously executes tasks needed to maintain trust across compliance, audits, risk management, vendor risk, privacy, and AI governance, enabling organizations to maintain a strong, reliable trust posture without draining operational bandwidth and resources on repetitive tasks. Backed by top-tier investors such as Accel, Elevation, and Blume Ventures, we’ve raised $31.8M in funding to fuel our mission. Trusted by over 4,000 organizations across 75 countries , Sprinto helps organizations stay audit-ready, manage real-time risks, and scale fearlessly. With 300+ native integrations and AI-driven automation, Sprinto supports 200+ global security standards natively , including SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and more. Sprinto 's extensible architecture enables organizations to build and support an infinite number of custom integrations and frameworks. Founded in 2020 by second-time founders Girish Redekar and Raghuveer Kancherla, Sprinto powers compliance for organizations like Whatfix, Encora, Anaconda, Whatnot, Ultrahuman, WeWork, Everstage, AI Foundation, HackerRank, and many more. Life as a Sprinter - Nobody succeeds at Sprinto by staying in their lane. We are organized around problems, not job titles. Sprinters take ownership beyond their role, solve hard problems, and care deeply about the impact they create. If something can be improved, fixed, or built, we don't wait for permission; we step in. Being remote means we rely less on proximity and more on trust. We write things down, communicate openly, and move quickly because great teams aren't built by sitting together, they're built by pulling in the same direction. We believe progress beats perfection, feedback is a gift, and doing the right thing matters, even when nobody is watching. And while we move with urgency, we never move alone. The mission - The Audit Experience function manages Sprinto ’s relationship with its audit partner ecosystem. This role offers a structured pathway to building genuine subject matter expertise in GRC and audit — not just theoretical familiarity, but the kind of depth that comes from working directly alongside an SME on real programs. The intern will engage hands-on with compliance frameworks like SOC 2 and ISO 27001, audit partner lifecycle management, and the product-led GRC environment that Sprinto operates in. This role is designed for someone who wants to develop into a domain expert in GRC and audit — you’ll build deep working knowledge of how audit programs function, how compliance controls are evaluated, and how information and cybersecurity requirements translate into real audit expectations. Day-to-day program support provides the applied context that accelerates this learning, grounding abstract frameworks in live, operational decisions. Where you'll leave your mark? Audit Partner Enablement Operations - Track and drive audit partners through the onboarding and enablement lifecycle. Maintain internal trackers, coordinate across teams to unblock dependencies, and flag partners stalling at any stage. Auditor Directory Maintenance - Keep the auditor directory accurate and current — verify accreditation status against relevant accreditation bodies, update partner profiles, and ensure listing information remains factually accurate. Evidence Mapping Support - Assist the SME in mapping audit evidence requirements to platform capabilities. This includes preparing reference data, identifying gaps, and documenting findings that feed into product improvement workflows. Audit Partner Vetting - Run the verification process for new audit partner candidates. Query Management - Serve as the first responder for routine auditor and internal team queries. Escalate non-routine matters to the SME. AI-Assisted Workflow Building - Build and iterate on AI agents to handle routine Audit Experience tasks — including audit partner queries, periodic auditor directory reviews, and evidence mapping lookups. Working with GenAI platforms such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini, you’ll design prompts, test agentic workflows, and help establish repeatable automation patterns that reduce manual effort over time. Ad Hoc Audit Experience Support - Assist the SME with other Audit Experience initiatives as they arise — including research, documentation, process improvement, and cross-functional coordination. The kind of builder we're looking for - Completed a graduation or master’s degree in GRC, Information Security, Risk Management, Computer Science, or a related field — candidates with an academic background directly in GRC or audit are strongly preferred Prior exposure to audits — whether through academic projects, internships, or professional experience — is a strong plus; candidates who have worked in or adjacent to audit functions are particularly encouraged to apply Genuine interest in exploring information and cybersecurity — you’re curious about how audit and compliance frameworks connect to real-world security posture, not just ticking boxes Comfortable working with spreadsheets, trackers, and data — a lot of the learning here happens through doing, not just observing Strong attention to detail — verification and mapping reviews are precision work Good written communication — you’ll be documenting processes and responding to audit partner queries Comfortable using GenAI tools — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or any equivalent platform; prior experience building agents or automating workflows with AI is a strong plus, but a genuine appetite to learn and experiment is what matters most Self-directed — the SME will provide guidance and review, but you’re expected to own the operational cadence independently How we care for our Sprinters? Work wherever you are : We are 100% remote, so you get to choose if you want to work from home, a cafe, the hills, or the beach. Co-working, on the house : If co-working is your jam, we offer a generous annual allowance. We care about your learning : We are invested in seeing you grow and commit USD 1,000 annually to help you level up your skills. We count your spark, not your leaves : Unlimited leave so you can reset when you need to. Your Safety Net, Woven In: Health insurance with coverage up to INR 10 lakh for you and your family, accident protection of an additional INR 10 lakh, and life insurance worth 3x your annual salary. Workspace setup of your dreams : We chip in INR 35,000 to help you build a setup that works for you. Inclusion & Diversity - At Sprinto , talent, curiosity, and ownership matter more than where you come from. We hire people for the problems they can solve, the impact they create, and the way they help others succeed—not their background, identity, or personal circumstances. We believe the best teams are built when people with different perspectives come together around a shared ambition to build something meaningful. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating a fair, inclusive, and accessible hiring process for everyone. Originally posted on Himalayas

title: Security Engineer (AI Red Team)
description: About Refractal Refractal is an AI security company building the infrastructure organisations need to defend against autonomous AI threats. 2026 has shown that generally capable intelligence is here. The challenge now is modernising security to stop AI-enabled threats, whether they come from internal agents going rogue or from attackers using AI to become more dangerous. Refractal was founded on cybersecurity and AI expertise from MIT, Microsoft, NASA and the U.S. Navy. Our product lets organisations detect AI-enabled threats at low cost without sacrificing detection quality. We take a practical approach to AI risk, combining proven cybersecurity methods with frontier AI security research. Today, we work with governments and organisations that can't afford to get security wrong. We're backed by leading deep-tech and cybersecurity investors and are growing the team to deliver on this mission. The role You'll test how deployed AI systems and agents fail under adversarial pressure. You'll run authorised, controlled security assessments, show what each finding means in practice, and work with our engineering and research teams to turn findings into stronger defences and repeatable tests. What you'll do Design and execute assessments of AI applications and agents, grounded in realistic attacker goals and clearly defined test scope. Test realistic threats such as indirect prompt injection, misuse of connected tools, sensitive data exposure and attempts to cross permission boundaries. Build reproducible test cases and small testing tools that demonstrate security impact and distinguish reliable failures from one-off outputs. Analyse how model behaviour, application design, identity and permissions combine to create vulnerabilities. Document findings, recommend practical mitigations and retest fixes with the engineers responsible for the affected systems. Success in your first six months You've established a repeatable assessment approach that connects realistic adversaries, test scenarios and security outcomes. You've produced actionable findings with reproducible evidence and helped validate the resulting fixes. You've built a growing set of regression tests that captures recurring failure modes and checks whether fixes hold. About you: essential Hands-on experience in offensive security, application security testing or adversarial testing of AI systems. A solid understanding of web applications, APIs, authentication, authorisation and common security failure modes. An understanding of how AI applications use prompts, retrieved information, memory and connected tools, and where trust boundaries arise. The ability to write code that automates testing, reproduces findings and inspects application behaviour. Good judgement around test scope and sensitive data, and the ability to explain technical findings in terms of practical impact. Nice to have Experience assessing LLM applications, agent workflows or systems that retrieve external content. Experience building security evaluation suites or testing proposed mitigations systematically. Experience combining application testing with cloud, identity or infrastructure security assessment. Our values Radical transparency. We believe the best work happens when everyone feels able to give and receive honest, constructive feedback. Public service. We see AI security as a form of public service. Getting the AI transition right means putting the right infrastructure in place to manage the threats that come with it, and our work helps protect the institutions and services society depends on. Fail fast. We test ideas early, seek feedback and learn quickly. We experiment rapidly and change course when something isn't working, without compromising on security. Pragmatism, not dogmatism. We choose approaches based on how well they solve the problem. That means combining established cybersecurity methods with frontier AI research, questioning our assumptions, and changing our minds when the evidence changes. title: Mission Critical Security Engineer – Threat Hunting
description: <p><strong>Help protect what truly matters in our customers' most critical environments by proactively identifying threats and improving how they are detected and addressed.</strong></p> <p>As a Mission Critical Security Engineer with a focus on Threat Hunting, you will be part of a dedicated customer team responsible for securing and continuously improving a complex, mission-critical application landscape.</p> <p>Working alongside other engineers and security specialists, you will help ensure the environment remains as secure and resilient as possible. You combine a strong engineering foundation with a security mindset, taking ownership of security improvements and understanding how systems, applications, and infrastructure behave.</p> <p>Your specific focus will be on threat hunting and detection engineering. Using your in-depth knowledge of the customer's technology stack and application landscape, you will fine-tune existing detection use cases and develop new ones tailored to the environment. You will use our custom SIEM/SOAR-based Managed Detection and Response (MDR) platform to turn emerging threats and technical insights into actionable detection capabilities.</p> <p>This role bridges security engineering, detection engineering, and threat intelligence. You don't simply follow predefined playbooks. You understand system behavior, identify gaps, and develop practical solutions that strengthen the security of the customer's environment.</p> <h2>/ What you will do</h2> <p><strong>Threat intelligence &amp; continuous improvement</strong></p> <ul data-spread="false"> <li> <p>Actively follow security developments, vulnerabilities, and threat intelligence and translate these into relevant hunts and detections.</p> </li> <li> <p>Identify security risks and gaps in detection coverage and proactively propose improvements.</p> </li> <li> <p>Use your knowledge of the customer's application and infrastructure landscape to continuously strengthen its security posture.</p> </li> <li> <p>Contribute to the evolution of the team's security monitoring and detection strategy.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Communication &amp; advisory</strong></p> <ul data-spread="false"> <li> <p>Translate findings into clear, actionable communication for engineers, customer stakeholders, and security specialists.</p> </li> <li> <p>Contribute to security advisories and share relevant threats across the customer team and wider organization.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work closely with engineers to understand system behavior and validate detection strategies.</p> </li> <li> <p>Collaborate with the customer's Security Operations Center (SOC) to align security monitoring, threat detection, and response activities.</p> </li> <li> <p>Help establish and improve integrations with the customer's SIEM/SOAR platform, including the forwarding of relevant logs and security telemetry.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Detection engineering &amp; threat hunting</strong></p> <ul data-spread="false"> <li> <p>Develop and continuously improve detection use cases based on emerging threats and observed behavior.</p> </li> <li> <p>Translate threat scenarios and security insights into actionable detection logic tailored to the customer's environment.</p> </li> <li> <p>Proactively perform threat hunting across the application and infrastructure landscape to identify abnormal or suspicious patterns.</p> </li> <li> <p>Analyze logs and telemetry data to uncover behaviors that are not yet covered by existing detections.</p> </li> <li> <p>Use your understanding of the customer's technology stack to distinguish normal from potentially malicious behavior.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Use case development &amp; response design</strong></p> <ul data-spread="false"> <li> <p>Define what should happen when detections trigger, including response actions, automation, and escalation paths.</p> </li> <li> <p>Continuously refine detection logic to improve quality, relevance, and signal-to-noise ratio.</p> </li> <li> <p>Build and fine-tune custom detection scenarios based on the specific characteristics and security requirements of the customer's environment.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Platform collaboration</strong></p> <ul data-spread="false"> <li> <p>Leverage our custom SIEM/SOAR-based MDR platform to implement detections and analyze data.</p> </li> <li> <p>Collaborate with platform and automation engineers to improve integrations and detection capabilities.</p> </li> <li> <p>Apply engineering and automation practices to ensure detection solutions are scalable, reliable, and maintainable.</p> </li> </ul> <h2>/ What you bring</h2> <p>We are looking for someone who combines solid engineering fundamentals with a strong interest in security and is motivated to move towards or deepen their expertise in threat hunting and detection engineering.</p> <p>You don't necessarily need to be an experienced threat hunter already. What matters is your ability to understand complex systems, recognize unusual behavior, and translate technical insights into practical security improvements.</p> <p><strong>Must-have skills</strong></p> <ul data-spread="false"> <li> <p>Solid engineering fundamentals, including Linux, networking, and infrastructure behavior.</p> </li> <li> <p>Hands-on experience with cloud environments such as AWS, Azure, or similar platforms.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with CI/CD, Git, and configuration management or infrastructure-as-code tooling.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong automation mindset and the ability to translate problems into scalable solutions.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience working with logs and telemetry to analyze system behavior and investigate technical issues.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with Python and/or Bash scripting.</p> </li> <li> <p>Familiarity with SIEM or log analytics platforms such as OpenSearch, Elastic, Splunk, or Microsoft Sentinel.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong understanding of security principles, including threat detection and response.</p> </li> <li> <p>Ability to distinguish normal from abnormal system behavior.</p> </li> <li> <p>Analytical, curious, and driven to understand how systems and threats behave.</p> </li> <li> <p>Ownership mindset, with responsibility for security quality and continuous improvement.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong communication skills to translate technical findings into actionable insights.</p> </li> <li> <p>Ability to connect business and customer context to technical security solutions.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice-to-have skills</strong></p> <ul data-spread="false"> <li> <p>Hands-on experience with threat hunting, detection engineering, or advanced SOC operations.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience developing or improving detection use cases and security monitoring rules.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with SOAR or security automation.</p> </li> <li> <p>Deep knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, Azure, and other Microsoft cloud services.</p> </li> <li> <p>Familiarity with threat intelligence frameworks such as MITRE ATT&amp;CK.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience integrating SIEM/SOAR platforms or forwarding security telemetry between different environments.</p> </li> </ul> <h2>/ Who are you?</h2> <p>You are an engineer with a strong interest in security, driven to understand how systems behave and how threats manifest.</p> <p>You don't follow playbooks blindly. You want to understand why detections exist, how systems interact, and where security can be improved.</p> <p>You combine analytical thinking with a hands-on mindset and enjoy working with complex applications, infrastructure, and data. You are curious, proactive, and take ownership of the quality of your work.</p> <p>You also enjoy being part of a customer team where security is a shared responsibility. You work closely with fellow engineers and security specialists, communicate clearly with stakeholders, and contribute to keeping the entire environment secure.</p> <h2>/ What can you expect?</h2> <p>At Schuberg Philis, you'll join a community of engineers with an awesome combination of exceptionally high security standards, an infatuation with automation, and the power to make a positive, sustainable impact on customers' business.</p> <p>You'll work within a dedicated customer team where engineers and security specialists jointly take responsibility for the security and reliability of mission-critical environments.</p> <p>Due to the nature of our customer engagements, there is no pressure on (billable) hours; we focus on quality and impact or how we like to call it:&nbsp;<strong>freedom &amp; responsibility</strong>. Ursprünglich für Mieterstrom in Gewerbeimmobilien entwickelt, unterstützt Solarize heute über 200 Unternehmen als Abrechnungslösung für PPAs, Mieterstrom, Wärme bis hin zu komplexen zeitreihenbasierten Energieprodukten im Geschäftskundenbereich. Das Solarize-Team besteht aus erfahrenen Gründern, Pionieren der Energiewende, Softwareexperten und hungrigen Macher:innen, die in einer offenen Kultur und im ständigen Austausch miteinander an den wichtigen Fragen der Energiewende arbeiten. Wir sind ausdauernd, wissbegierig, veränderungswillig und unbequem. So verändern wir den Energiesektor hin zu einer kundenorientierten und innovativen Branche und leisten dadurch unseren Beitrag für die zentralen Herausforderungen unserer Zeit. Energieversorger vertrauen uns ihre Abrechnungsdaten an. Deshalb ist Informationssicherheit bei uns Teil des Produkts. Für unser Büro in Berlin suchen wir eine:n Werkstudent:in ISMS & Compliance (m/w/d) , der:die unser nach ISO/IEC 27001:2022 zertifiziertes ISMS mitgestaltet und weiterentwickelt. Aufgaben Deine Mission bei uns Du sorgst mit dafür, dass die Plattform für die Energiewende sicher bleibt. Dabei lernst du Informationssicherheit so kennen, wie sie in einem wachsenden SaaS-Unternehmen tatsächlich gelebt wird. Halte unser ISMS auditfest: Du unterstützt dabei, die Anforderungen der ISO/IEC 27001:2022 im Alltag umzusetzen und zu überprüfen. Du pflegst Richtlinien, Nachweise und Risikobewertungen und begleitest interne und externe Audits aus erster Reihe. Mach Sicherheit messbar: Du definierst aussagekräftige KPIs für unser ISMS, erhebst sie möglichst automatisiert und machst sie in Dashboards sichtbar. Aus den Zahlen leitest du konkrete Verbesserungen ab. Entwickle das ISMS weiter: Du bringst eigene Ideen ein, wie Prozesse schlanker, Kontrollen wirksamer und Dokumentation hilfreicher werden. Dein Ziel ist ein ISMS, das im Arbeitsalltag unterstützt und auch gelebt wird. Sichere unsere Geräteflotte: Du gestaltest das Mobile Device Management unserer Firmengeräte aktiv mit, von Sicherheitsrichtlinien und Konfigurationsprofilen bis zum Rollout für mobile Geräte. Gestalte Information Security im KI-Zeitalter: Du findest Antworten auf eine der spannendsten Fragen unserer Branche: Wie setzen wir KI-Tools produktiv ein und schützen gleichzeitig die Daten unserer Kunden zuverlässig? Dafür entwickelst du Richtlinien, Freigabeprozesse und technische Leitplanken, die Sicherheit und Effizienz verbinden. Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe: Du arbeitest eng mit unserem Engineering-Team und den Verantwortlichen für Informationssicherheit zusammen und übersetzt Sicherheitsanforderungen in praktikable Lösungen. Qualifikation Wir glauben fest daran, dass die richtige Einstellung und Motivation oft wichtiger sind als ein lückenloser Lebenslauf. Das bringst du mit (Must-haves): Studium mit Tech-Fokus: Du studierst Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik, (IT-)Sicherheit, Security Management oder einen vergleichbaren Studiengang, zum Beispiel an der TU Berlin, HTW, BHT oder am HPI in Potsdam. Echtes Interesse an Informationssicherheit: Du hast erste Berührungspunkte gesammelt, etwa über Vorlesungen, Projekte, CTFs oder dein eigenes Homelab, und willst wissen, wie Security in der Praxis funktioniert. Technisches Grundverständnis: Du verstehst, wie Cloud-Infrastruktur, Identitäts- und Zugriffsmanagement und Endgeräte zusammenspielen. Mit Python, Bash oder TypeScript automatisierst du wiederkehrende Aufgaben. KI-gestützte Arbeitsweise: Du nutzt KI-Tools gezielt, prüfst ihre Ergebnisse kritisch und hast ein Gespür dafür, welche Daten in welches Tool gehören. Struktur und Sorgfalt: Du arbeitest gewissenhaft, behältst auch bei vielen Anforderungen den Überblick und schreibst Dokumentation, die andere gerne lesen. Zeit für uns: Du kannst 15–20 Stunden pro Woche in der Vorlesungszeit einplanen, idealerweise für mindestens 12 Monate. Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse: Du kommunizierst sicher in beiden Sprachen, im Team ebenso wie mit Auditoren. Pluspunkte sammelst du mit (Nice-to-haves): Framework-Wissen: Du hast dich bereits mit ISO 27001, BSI IT-Grundschutz oder NIS2 beschäftigt. title: Data Enablement Officer
description: At Efficio, we're not just a consulting firm; we're a team of dedicated experts committed to transforming procurement and supply chain functions. Our mission is to drive sustainable, measurable value for our clients through innovative solutions and deep industry insights. Join us and be part of a dynamic environment where your skills and ideas make a real impact. Efficio is the world’s largest specialist procurement and supply chain consultancy, with offices across Europe, North America, and the Middle East. We’re a diverse team of over 1,000 individuals, representing more than 60 different nationalities and speaking 40+ languages – and we’re continuing to grow rapidly! Data Enablement Officer Help shape how Efficio uses data responsibly, securely and effectively. We are looking for a Data Enablement Officer to establish and lead Efficio’s data governance framework, helping us protect client data while enabling its responsible use across our services, analytics, products and AI capabilities. This is a highly visible role at the intersection of data, technology, AI, risk and client delivery. You will work across the business to turn complex contractual, regulatory, privacy and security requirements into practical guidance that enables teams to innovate with confidence. Initially, the role will have a strong advisory and enablement focus: helping teams understand client requirements, assess new uses of data and make proportionate, risk-based decisions. As our governance model matures, the role is expected to take greater ownership of the framework and delegated authority for lower-risk decisions. What you'll be doing Establish our data governance framework You will assess our current data-handling practices and develop a practical, scalable governance framework covering the lifecycle of client data – from collection and classification through to access, use, sharing, storage, retention and secure deletion. You will develop and maintain policies and standards covering areas including: Client data handling and classification Data reuse and fair usage Use of client data within Efficio products Use of data with AI tools, including third-party and self-hosted solutions Data access and security Retention, archiving and secure disposal Anonymisation and aggregation Third-party data sharing Policy exceptions and escalation You will also help establish and maintain our information asset inventories, data flows and AI asset registers. Enable responsible use of data and AI A key part of the role will be helping teams determine what we can do with data, under what conditions, and with what safeguards. You will establish a consistent approach for assessing new and changing data use cases, considering factors such as: Why the data was originally obtained Client and contractual restrictions Data sensitivity and classification The proposed use and intended recipients Security and access controls Retention requirements Legal, client and reputational considerations For AI use cases, you will help define which activities are permitted, restricted, require additional review or are prohibited. This will include the use of prompts, uploaded files and connected data sources, as well as expectations around human oversight, output validation and accountability. Govern products, platforms and technology You will define the conditions under which client data can be stored or processed using Efficio products, SaaS platforms, cloud services and AI tools. Working closely with Technology, Information Security, Legal and Privacy teams, you will assess areas including: Data residency and international transfers Encryption, access controls and logging Supplier and subcontractor access Data retention, backups and deletion Exit and data-export arrangements Use of customer data for AI model training, product improvement or other secondary purposes You will help ensure that unapproved platforms are not used for client data without appropriate assessment and documented approval. Support new solutions and innovation You will work alongside teams designing and deploying new data, software, analytics and AI solutions, providing governance input from an early stage. Ahead of launch, you will help confirm that the appropriate governance, legal, privacy and security reviews have taken place and that material risks have been appropriately addressed. Where issues remain, you will recommend practical remediation, escalation or, where necessary, a delay to rollout. Acceptance of significant residual risk will remain with the appropriate executive or governance committee. Build governance that works in practice This role isn't simply about writing policies. We want to create a governance model that teams can understand and use. You will help develop: A clear data governance operating model and decision-rights framework Practical data, AI, security, reuse and retention policies Data and AI use-case assessment processes Risk-classification and escalation models Policy exception processes and decision registers Product and AI platform assessment standards Solution launch-readiness checklists Training, guidance and supporting materials Governance reporting for senior leadership and relevant committees You will coordinate, advise and constructively challenge stakeholders across the organisation while recognising that responsibility for managing data risk is shared across business owners, data owners, Legal and Privacy, Information Security, Technology and senior governance forums. Client engagement This will also be an important client-facing role. You will participate in client discussions where required, confidently explaining Efficio's approach to data governance, security and responsible data use. You should be comfortable responding to questions about how client data is accessed, used, stored, shared, retained and protected, translating technical or governance concepts into clear, credible explanations for different audiences. What we're looking for We are looking for someone with experience across one or more of the following areas: Data governance or data management Data privacy Information security Technology or operational risk AI governance or responsible AI You will also bring a practical understanding of modern technology environments, including SaaS, cloud, analytics and AI platforms. You'll be someone who can operate comfortably between policy and practice – able to understand complex requirements while recognising the commercial and operational realities of a consulting and technology-enabled business. In particular, you will be able to: Translate complex regulatory, contractual and security requirements into practical business guidance Apply proportionate, risk-based judgement rather than relying on a purely rules-based approach Influence and challenge senior stakeholders constructively Work effectively across Technology, Security, Legal, Privacy and business teams Balance commercial objectives and innovation with appropriate governance Communicate confidently with clients and senior internal stakeholders Build processes and frameworks that are robust without creating unnecessary bureaucracy Navigate emerging areas where the answer may not always be immediately clear What success looks like Success in this role will mean that teams understand how to use data appropriately rather than simply being told what they cannot do. We will look at measures including adoption of priority policies, review turnaround times, reduction in unapproved tool usage, effective management of exceptions, quality of governance reporting, stakeholder feedback and a reduction in recurring governance issues. Ultimately, the role will be judged on its ability to achieve both sides of our data ambition: protecting our clients and Efficio while enabling appropriate, secure and innovative use of data and AI. title: NATOIS-0052 Cloud Engineer (NS) - THU 12 Nov
description: Deadline Date: Thursday 12 November 2026 Requirement: Cloud Engineer Location: Brussels, BE Full Time On-Site: No Time On-Site: 40% Total Scope of the request (hours): Base period 2027: 38 hours/week for a total of 42 weeks and a total of 1596 hours 2028 Option: 38 hours/week for a total of 42 weeks and a total of 1596 hours Period of Performance: 2027 BASE: 18 Jan 2027 to 31 Dec 2027 2028 Option: 01 Jan – 31 Dec 2028 Required Security Clearance: NATO SECRET Special Terms and Conditions: The contractor will be responsible for complying with the respective national requirements for working permits, visas, taxes social security etc. whilst working on site at NATO HQ- Brussels, Belgium. No special status is either conferred or implied by the host organisation, NATO HQ- Brussels, Belgium on to the contractor whilst working on site. 1 GENERAL 1.1 Introduction 1.1.1 The Cyber Threat Analysis Branch (CTAB) is looking for a Cloud Engineer to further develop and maintain the cloud environment used to host NATO’s cyber threat intelligence platform, intended to support cyber threat intelligence production for the NATO Enterprise and Alliance. 1.2 Background Information 1.2.1 The Joint Intelligence and Security Division (JISD), under the leadership of the Assistant Secretary General for Intelligence and Security (ASG I&S), comprises two principal pillars: Intelligence – headed by the Deputy ASG for Intelligence; and the NATO Office of Security (NOS) – headed by the Deputy ASG for Security. Intelligence is responsible for ensuring the situational awareness of the North Atlantic Council and the Military Committee, for the analysis of the indications and warnings in support of the NATO Crisis Response System and for the development of intelligence policies and capabilities for NATO. Its functional areas address: intelligence analysis and production, intelligence policy and capability development. 1.2.2 The joint civilian and military Intelligence Production Unit (IPU), under the JISD, delivers strategic intelligence-based analysis to support North Atlantic Council (NAC) and Military Committee (MC) decision making on strategic issues of concern. The IPU produces a range of planned and tasked intelligence products on regional issues in Eurasia, Africa and the Middle East, and on transnational issues such as hybrid warfare, terrorism, instability, weapons of mass destruction and energy security. 1.2.3 The Cyber Threat Analysis Branch (CTAB), under the IPU, is responsible for providing evidence-based assessments of the cyber threat landscape to empower NATO stakeholders to make risk-informed decisions. The multidisciplinary team combines all-source data with cutting edge technologies to support and enhance the Alliance leaderships’ understanding on the nature of cyber competition and conflict. CTAB systematically identifies strategic patterns and trends in cyber space and generates tailored insights to support network defence and mission assurance with predictive analysis, cyber threat intelligence, and threat hunting. 2 STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES 2.1 Corporate Objective 2.2 The contractor (Cloud Engineer) will support the work of the Cyber Threat Analysis Branch and be responsible for maintain and developing CTAB’s cloud environment in order to support the functioning of CTAB’s cyber threat intelligence platform. 2.3 Contract Objective 2.3.1 Obtain specialist consulting services to support the following initiatives: 2.3.1.1 Ensure the integrity, availability and confidentiality of CTAB’s cloud environment and lead maintenance and development efforts together with a software engineer, data scientist, and CTI researchers. 2.3.1.2 Push for innovative new ways to architect security, data flows, and cost optimalization within the environment while ensuring maximum stability, scalability and functionality. 2.3.1.3 Develop automation pipelines for infrastructure provisioning and configuration as well as for coding projects within the platform, while ensuring up-to-date documentation and clear communications on performed work. 2.3.1.4. Help in transitioning from a AWS-based cloud environment to a Azure-based cloud environment. 2.4 Management Objective 2.4.1 Allow the Contractor the maximum flexibility to innovatively manage its corporate resources and expertise so as to provide a high-value contribution in support to NATO’s corporate and contract objectives within existing constraints and available funding. 3 PERSONNEL AND RESOURCES [See Requirements] 4 HOURS OF OPERATION 4.1 While performing at NATO sites, Contractor’s personnel must work during NATO official working hours (normally between 8:30–18:00, Monday to Thursday, and between 8:30-16:00 on Friday), unless otherwise specified in the task orders. Recognized holidays are official holidays approved by the NATO site specified in the task order, or if no site is specified in the task order, by the NATO Headquarters. A list of the official holidays can be obtained from the NATO Project Manager designated in task orders. 4.2 Exceptionally, Contractor’s personnel may be required to work outside normal working hours. 4.3 Exceptionally, Contractor’s personnel may be required to visit other locations other than those specified in the task order in order to participate in project-related meetings, in which case any associated travel costs will be reimbursed. 4.4 Contractor’s Key Personnel performing services under Contract shall take vacation and voluntary leave at times agreed between the Contractor and the designated NATO Project Manager. 5 NATO FURNISHED PROPERTY AND SERVICES 5.1 The Organization will provide the Contractor with a secure working environment in NATO HQ for an expected minimum of 2 days per week, where the other 3 days per week are remote work from home, as well as access to the CTAB cyber threat intelligence platform. 6 CONTRACTOR FURNISHED PROPERTY AND SERVICES 6.1 Except for those items or services specifically stated to be NATO furnished in Section 5 above, the Contractor shall furnish everything required to perform this Contract. 7 CONTRACTOR TASKS 7.1 General 7.1.1 Under the guidance and supervision of the NATO IS Procurement Service, the selected service provider will be responsible for the execution of the tasks and for the delivery of the specialist products specified in this SOW. 7.2 Task Order Management 7.2.1 The Contractor will be responsible for conducting cloud engineering to support NATO’s cyber threat intelligence production. The Contractor must: 7.2.1.1 Ensure the availability, confidentiality, and integrity of CTAB’s cloud environment, and do so in a cost-effective way, by provisioning, configuring and monitoring cloud resources using Terraform and ensure all code and work is maintainable and documented. 7.2.1.2 Work with data scientists, software engineers, researchers and end-users to translate their requirements into functionalities within the cloud environment, while ensuring security is front-and-centre. 7.2.1.3 Participate in team and branch calls as required by the team lead to give status updates on projects and developments pertinent to the Contractor’s tasks. 7.3 Development of Specialist Products 7.3.1 The Contractor shall produce the Deliverables as specified in the task order management under supervision of the NATO Project Manager. The Contractor shall submit Deliverables to the NATO Project Manager for Quality Review, test or inspection not later than the dates specified by the NATO Project Manager. 7.3.2 The Contractor shall continuously validate any deliverables with the NATO Project Manager and peers within CTAB. 7.3.3 The Contractor shall hold periodic sessions with the NATO Project Manager to make sure that the deliverables are aligned with NATO’s expectations. 8 QUALITY CONTROL 8.1 Contractor’s products must comply with the criteria as set forth by the NATO Project Manager. Contractor must implement an appropriate quality control process in order to make sure that the products which are submitted for quality review, inspection or acceptance are of acceptable quality. 8.2 The Organization will immediately stop the review, inspection, acceptance or delivery of those products or services that are affected by material deficiencies, significant omissions, or gross mistakes and return the delinquent products to the Contractor for correction, or request the reperformance of service. The review and acceptance processes will be suspended until the Contractor’s shows that the product has been subject to a thorough quality control before being submitted again for review. 9 QUALITY ASSURANCE AND CONTRACTOR PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT 9.1 General 9.1.1 NATO will evaluate the Contractor’s performance under this task order in accordance with reasonable quality assurance procedures and techniques such as random and periodic inspections and surveys. All observations will be recorded by NATO Project Manager or his/her designees. When an observation indicates defective performance, the NATO Project Manager will obtain the Contractor’s representative’s initials on the record of the observation. Contract Discrepancy Reports will be issued wherever the nature and circumstances of the deficiency warrant such a measure. 9.2 Performance Evaluation Meetings 9.2.1 The Contractor’s contract or project manager may be required to meet periodically with the NATO Project Manager and the Procurement Officer during the period of task order performance. Meetings will be scheduled as required. The Contractor may request meetings whenever a Contract Discrepancy Report is issued. The written minutes of these meetings shall be signed by the contractor’s manager, Procurement Officer, and NATO Project Manager. If the Contractor does not concur with the minutes, any areas of non-concurrence shall be submitted to NATO Project Manager within 10 working days of receipt of the signed minutes. 3 PERSONNEL AND RESOURCES 3.1 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 3.1.1 All general and domain specific qualification requirements stated in the AAS+ Framework Agreement shall be applicable (e.g., required English proficiency). The Contractor will require a NATO SECRET clearance. 3.2 SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS 3.2.1 In addition to the generic qualification requirements established in the AAS+ Agreement, The Contractor must have: A university degree from a nationally recognised/certified university in a quantitative discipline (Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Operations Research, etc.) with substantial systems engineering content and 2 years of specific experience – OR - at least 4 years’ experience similar to the tasks described in this SoW and relevant industry recognized certificates. Knowledge of and experience in maintaining and developing multi-account AWS cloud environments, specifically in core AWS products such as Lambda, S3, CloudTrail, ECS, EC2, and similar, as well as working according to industry best practices such as AWS’s Well Architected Framework. Significant experience in using Terraform to build and maintain cloud infrastructure as code, setting up CI/CD pipelines, automating containerized workloads on ECS and conditional access. Able to set up monitoring, logging and alerting with tools like CloudTrail and GuardDuty, and experienced in managing IAM with SSO, VPC networking, and least-privilege security controls. Proficient in Python and Bash and knowledge of Docker, Linux administration and Git. Experience within cybersecurity and/or the intelligence domain is strongly preferred but not required for this role, as is experience with Azure. Good communication skills, both orally and written. Able to translate complex technical topics into information conveyable to non-domain experts. Can easily cooperate with non-cloud experts and explain conducted work, as well as give and take feedback and create clear and structured documentation based on the work conducted.

description: Deadline Date: Thursday 12 November 2026 Requirement: Cyber Threat Intelligence Researcher Location: Brussels, BE Full Time On-Site: No Time On-Site: 40% Total Scope of the request (hours): Base period 2027: 38 hours/week for a total of 42 weeks and a total of 1596 hours 2028 Option: 38 hours/week for a total of 42 weeks and a total of 1596 hours Period of Performance: 2027 BASE: 18 Jan 2027 to 31 Dec 2027 2028 Option: 01 Jan – 31 Dec 2028 Required Security Clearance: NATO SECRET Special Terms and Conditions: The contractor will be responsible for complying with the respective national requirements for working permits, visas, taxes social security etc. whilst working on site at NATO HQ- Brussels, Belgium. No special status is either conferred or implied by the host organisation, NATO HQ- Brussels, Belgium on to the contractor whilst working on site. 1 GENERAL 1.1 Introduction 1.1.1 The Cyber Threat Analysis Branch (CTAB) is looking for a Cyber Threat Intelligence Researcher to support in the provision of technical cyber threat intelligence to the NATO Enterprise and Alliance through researching threat actors’ tactics, techniques and procedures. 1.2 Background Information 1.2.1 The Joint Intelligence and Security Division (JISD), under the leadership of the Assistant Secretary General for Intelligence and Security (ASG I&S), comprises two principal pillars: Intelligence – headed by the Deputy ASG for Intelligence; and the NATO Office of Security (NOS) – headed by the Deputy ASG for Security. Intelligence is responsible for ensuring the situational awareness of the North Atlantic Council and the Military Committee, for the analysis of the indications and warnings in support of the NATO Crisis Response System and for the development of intelligence policies and capabilities for NATO. Its functional areas address: intelligence analysis and production, intelligence policy and capability development. 1.2.2 The joint civilian and military Intelligence Production Unit (IPU), under the JISD, delivers strategic intelligence-based analysis to support North Atlantic Council (NAC) and Military Committee (MC) decision making on strategic issues of concern. The IPU produces a range of planned and tasked intelligence products on regional issues in Eurasia, Africa and the Middle East, and on transnational issues such as hybrid warfare, terrorism, instability, weapons of mass destruction and energy security. 1.2.3 The Cyber Threat Analysis Branch (CTAB), under the IPU, is responsible for providing evidence-based assessments of the cyber threat landscape to empower NATO stakeholders to make risk-informed decisions. The multidisciplinary team combines all-source data with cutting edge technologies to support and enhance the Alliance leaderships’ understanding on the nature of cyber competition and conflict. CTAB systematically identifies strategic patterns and trends in cyber space and generates tailored insights to support network defence and mission assurance with predictive analysis, cyber threat intelligence, and threat hunting. 2 STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES 2.1 Corporate Objective 2.2 The contractor (Cyber Threat Intelligence Researcher) will support the work of the Cyber Threat Analysis Branch and help conduct research into threat actors’ tactics, techniques and procedures – and will create accurate, actionable and relevant technical reporting of interest to the Alliance. 2.3 Contract Objective 2.3.1 Obtain specialist consulting services to support the following initiatives: 2.3.1.1 Create scripts and queries to accurately and automatically track threat actor infrastructure and tools using commercial and open-source information and tools; 2.3.1.2 Write technical threat intelligence products, including detection signatures, meant for network defenders to aid network defence, threat hunting and adversary emulation efforts; 2.3.1.3 Aid in translating technical cyber threat intelligence into operational and strategic intelligence products to inform decision-makers at NATO. 2.4 Management Objective 2.4.1 Allow the Contractor the maximum flexibility to innovatively manage its corporate resources and expertise so as to provide a high-value contribution in support to the NATO’s corporate and contract objectives within existing constraints and available funding. 3 PERSONNEL AND RESOURCES [See Requirements] 4 HOURS OF OPERATION 4.1 While performing at NATO sites, Contractor’s personnel must work during NATO official working hours (normally between 8:30–18:00, Monday to Thursday, and between 8:30-16:00 on Friday), unless otherwise specified in the task orders. Recognized holidays are official holidays approved by the NATO site specified in the task order, or if no site is specified in the task order, by the NATO Headquarters. A list of the official holidays can be obtained from the NATO Project Manager designated in task orders. 4.2 Exceptionally, Contractor’s personnel may be required to work outside normal working hours. 4.3 Exceptionally, Contractor’s personnel may be required to visit other locations other than those specified in the task order in order to participate in project-related meetings, in which case any associated travel costs will be reimbursed. 4.4 Contractor’s Key Personnel performing services under Contract shall take vacation and voluntary leave at times agreed between the Contractor and the designated NATO Project Manager. 5 NATO FURNISHED PROPERTY AND SERVICES 5.1 The Organization will provide the Contractor with a secure working environment in NATO HQ for an expected minimum of 2 days per week, where the other 3 days per week are remote work from home, as well as access to the CTAB cyber threat intelligence platform. 6 CONTRACTOR FURNISHED PROPERTY AND SERVICES 6.1 Except for those items or services specifically stated to be NATO furnished in Section 5 above, the Contractor shall furnish everything required to perform this Contract. 7 CONTRACTOR TASKS 7.1 General 7.1.1 Under the guidance and supervision of the NATO IS Procurement Service, the selected service provider will be responsible for the execution of the tasks and for the delivery of the specialist products specified in this SOW. 7.2 Task Order Management 7.2.1 The Contractor will be responsible for conducting cloud engineering to support NATO’s cyber threat intelligence production. The Contractor must: 7.2.1.1 Use the CTAB Cyber Threat Intelligence Platform and other sources to conduct research into prioritized cyber threat actors to discover new infrastructure and capabilities under the direction of the team lead. Conduct pattern analysis on threat actor infrastructure to detect new malicious infrastructure, and script and automate that detection to allow for threat intelligence at scale. Find and analyse potential new cyber threats to NATO based on existing or novel techniques and scripts, and correlate with all available sources to establish an adequate threat picture. 7.2.1.3 Translate threat actor tactics, techniques and procedures into actionable intelligence for 1) network defenders through creating detection signatures, contextualizing IoC’s, and writing standardized CTI products, and 2) strategic cyber analysts for use in intelligence production to decision makers. Support other threat researchers in their activities, and advise and assist strategic cyber threat analysts in understanding complex technical topics. 7.2.1.4 Participate in team and branch calls as required by the team lead to give status updates on projects and developments pertinent to the Contractor’s tasks, and ensure constant delivery of findings, mostly comprising indicators of compromise and MITRE techniques, on novel threat actors. Equally deliver scripts and methodologies that improve on current processes and tooling and enhance NATO’s ability to track adversaries in cyberspace. 7.3 Development of Specialist Products 7.3.1 The Contractor shall produce the Deliverables as specified in the task order management under supervision of the NATO Project Manager. The Contractor shall submit Deliverables to the NATO Project Manager for Quality Review, test or inspection not later than the dates specified by the NATO Project Manager. 7.3.2 The Contractor shall continuously validate any deliverables with the NATO Project Manager and peers within CTAB. 7.3.3 The Contractor shall hold periodic sessions with the NATO Project Manager to make sure that the deliverables are aligned with NATO’s expectations. 8 QUALITY CONTROL 8.1 Contractor’s products must comply with the criteria as set forth by the NATO Project Manager. Contractor must implement an appropriate quality control process in order to make sure that the products which are submitted for quality review, inspection or acceptance are of acceptable quality. 8.2 The Organization will immediately stop the review, inspection, acceptance or delivery of those products or services that are affected by material deficiencies, significant omissions, or gross mistakes and return the delinquent products to the Contractor for correction, or request the reperformance of service. The review and acceptance processes will be suspended until the Contractor’s shows that the product has been subject to a thorough quality control before being submitted again for review. 9 QUALITY ASSURANCE AND CONTRACTOR PERFORMANCE ASSESSMENT 9.1 General 9.1.1 NATO will evaluate the Contractor’s performance under this task order in accordance with reasonable quality assurance procedures and techniques such as random and periodic inspections and surveys. All observations will be recorded by NATO Project Manager or his/her designees. When an observation indicates defective performance, the NATO Project Manager will obtain the Contractor’s representative’s initials on the record of the observation. Contract Discrepancy Reports will be issued wherever the nature and circumstances of the deficiency warrant such a measure. 9.2 Performance Evaluation Meetings 9.2.1 The Contractor’s contract or project manager may be required to meet periodically with the NATO Project Manager and the Procurement Officer during the period of task order performance. Meetings will be scheduled as required. The Contractor may request meetings whenever a Contract Discrepancy Report is issued. The written minutes of these meetings shall be signed by the contractor’s manager, Procurement Officer, and NATO Project Manager. If the Contractor does not concur with the minutes, any areas of non-concurrence shall be submitted to NATO Project Manager within 10 working days of receipt of the signed minutes. 3 PERSONNEL AND RESOURCES 3.1 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 3.1.1 All general and domain specific qualification requirements stated in the AAS+ Framework Agreement shall be applicable (e.g., required English proficiency). The Contractor will require a NATO SECRET clearance. 3.2 SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS 3.2.1 In addition to the generic qualification requirements established in the AAS+ Agreement, The Contractor must have: A university degree from a nationally recognised/certified university in a quantitative discipline (Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, Operations Research, etc.) with substantial computer science content and 2 years of specific experience – OR - at least 4 years’ experience similar to the tasks described in this SoW and relevant industry recognized certificates. Knowledge and experience in analysis of various threat actor groups, attack patterns and tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) to produce actionable threat intelligence to enable network and host defences in organizations with demonstrable impact. Experience with and knowledge of the intelligence lifecycle, analytical tradecraft and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK. Good communication skills, both orally and written. Able to translate complex technical topics into information conveyable to non-domain experts. Can easily cooperate with other threat researchers by taking and giving feedback Knowledge of network and system fundamentals and experience in any of the following cybersecurity fields: network monitoring, threat hunting, incident response, red teaming, host/network forensics, or reverse engineering. Experience with programming in scripting languages such as Python

INTRODUCTION The BICES (Battlefield Information Collection and Exploitation Systems) is an association of independent elements to enable the sharing and exchange of timely intelligence-related information between all NATO member nations, associated partner nations and the NATO organization. BICES capabilities are intended for national, NATO or coalition use, during peace, crisis and war, supporting decision-makers, deployed force commanders and tactical users. The BICES Group Executive (BGX) works as a facilitator maintaining the core network and coordinating the community-wide provision of capabilities and services operated at national/organisational level. BICES offers a number of services to support BICES users using mainly commercial off-the-shelf (COTS), open source but also an in-house developed software. Within BGX, the BICES Support Unit (BSU) is responsible for managing the BICES services across the BICES NATO HQ Element that includes the following CIS functional areas by providing daily operational support: BGX Service Desk, Networking/Communications, Secure Voice & Video telecommunications platforms and Systems/Applications services, SharePoint, Call Manager support. Additionally, the BSU provides general maintenance functions, and quality assurance, and manages customer feedback. The BSU provides support related to IT Incidents, problems and service requests to the BICES NATO HQ Element users. The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to engage external contractor to staff the BSU. 2. JOB DESCRIPTION Under the supervision of the BSU Chief and in close coordination with the BGX Security Officers and Engineers, the incumbent provides 2nd level support for complex technical cybersecurity-based activities in the area of CIS monitoring and security incident response. S/He contributes to the day-to-day CIS security testing, verifications, scanning, monitoring, updating, baselining, improving and documenting activities of the cybersecurity capabilities implemented within the BICES NATO HQ Element networks. The incumbent reports the status and the discoveries of the security posture of BICES NATO HQ Element networks and contributes to the monitoring, analysis and modifications of security services. The incumbent may be required to undertake operational deployments and/or travel duty assignments both within and beyond NATO's boundaries. The work is performed in a typical Secure Facility environment where slightly undesirable conditions may apply. The risk of injury is categorized as: Light Risk of Injury. 3. LOCATION OF DUTY The location of duty is on-site at the NATO HQ offices in Brussels, Belgium. 4. TIMELINES The base period of performance is 4th January 2027 to 31st December. If the 2028 option is exercised, the period of performance is 1 January 2028 to 31 December 2028. 5. TRAVEL Occasional business travel may be required. Travel expenses will be reimbursed to the individual directly (in addition to the hourly rate) under NATO rules. 6. SECURITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT The contractor must be in possession of a NATO COSMIC TOP SECRET security clearance. A signed Non-Disclosure Agreement will be required as per Annex C. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE Essential The incumbent must: Possess higher secondary education with at least 3 years post related experience and possess at least 1 year post-related experience in CIS security activities; Possess at least 1 year of experience in Windows and Linux based operating systems and platforms, of update service platforms and technologies and of IP based networking and devices; Possess at least 1 year of experience in firewall and intrusion detection technologies; Demonstrate the ability to identify and describe computer and network anomalies within a CIS and to understand, assess and solve technical issues; Possess at least 1 year of experience in security tools such as firewalls, proxies, guard technology, SIEM solutions and scanning tools; Possess at least 1 year of experience in Security Operations Centre (SOC) processes and procedures; Possess at least 1 year of experience invulnerability assessment and penetration testing techniques, log fusion and log analysis capabilities; Be able to communicate effectively orally and in writing; Be flexible to work outside regular office hours; Possess level V (Advanced) of the English language. Desirable The following will be considered an advantage: Knowledge of NATO security policies and supporting directives; Experience working in a multinational environment; Familiarity with NATO structure and procedures; Experience with the application of techniques/methods for source verification, data fusion, quality analysis, and threat actor profiling. title: Systems Engineer
description: About Refractal Refractal is an AI security company building the infrastructure organisations need to defend against autonomous AI threats. 2026 has shown that generally capable intelligence is here. The challenge now is modernising security to stop AI-enabled threats, whether they come from internal agents going rogue or from attackers using AI to become more dangerous. Refractal was founded on cybersecurity and AI expertise from MIT, Microsoft, NASA and the U.S. Navy. Our product lets organisations detect AI-enabled threats at low cost without sacrificing detection quality. We take a practical approach to AI risk, combining proven cybersecurity methods with frontier AI security research. Today, we work with governments and organisations that can't afford to get security wrong. We're backed by leading deep-tech and cybersecurity investors and are growing the team to deliver on this mission. The role Own the services and infrastructure that keep Refractal secure and reliable in production. You will work across the enforcement runtime, data integrity, tenant isolation, agent tracing, model services, and cloud infrastructure. Build systems that connect activity across agents, services, and tools, evaluate risk, apply decisions, and preserve the evidence behind them. What you'll work on Build and operate a low-latency runtime enforcement pipeline with predictable failure behaviour. Own observability and tracing across agent actions, tool calls, model calls, and enforcement decisions. Build tamper-evident evidence storage and enforce multi-tenant isolation throughout every data path. Create reliable event and streaming services with safe handling for load, retries, backpressure, and disconnections. Build infrastructure for red-team jobs, evaluation workloads, and model-serving services. Own cloud infrastructure, continuous delivery, secrets, artefact verification, and production trust boundaries. What we're looking for A systems engineer who reasons carefully about latency, failure, isolation, integrity, and cost, and uses measurements rather than assumptions. Strong experience with backend, distributed, or infrastructure systems; Python experience is preferred. Production observability and distributed tracing experience, ideally with OpenTelemetry or similar tooling. Experience building responsive services under load with correct timeout, retry, and backpressure behaviour. Experience with Postgres, Row-Level Security, migrations, and multi-tenant access-control testing. Hands-on experience with containers, cloud infrastructure, continuous delivery, and operational security. The ability to work independently and own technically ambiguous production problems. Our values Radical transparency. We believe the best work happens when everyone feels able to give and receive honest, constructive feedback. Public service. We see AI security as a form of public service. Getting the AI transition right means putting the right infrastructure in place to manage the threats that come with it, and our work helps protect the institutions and services society depends on. Fail fast. We test ideas early, seek feedback and learn quickly. We experiment rapidly and change course when something isn't working, without compromising on security. Pragmatism, not dogmatism. We choose approaches based on how well they solve the problem. That means combining established cybersecurity methods with frontier AI research, questioning our assumptions, and changing our minds when the evidence changes. What we offer Competitive salary, meaningful equity, and a performance-linked bonus. Direct influence over the product, architecture, engineering standards, and company direction. A clear path to technical leadership as the engineering team grows. London-based, in-person work, with UK Skilled Worker visa sponsorship and support for Global Talent applications.
