We are seeking an AI Systems Infrastructure Engineer (IC4) to lead the platform and backend architecture powering our real-time security detection services. In this role, you will build and scale low-latency serving infrastructure for Small Language Models (SLM), Prompt Injection (PI) engines, and Content / Intent Classification platforms running across GPU and cloud clusters. We are looking for a strong systems engineer who understands production backend services, microservices, container management, and high-throughput inference optimization. While you will work closely with ML researchers, your primary focus will be engineering robust backend services, GPU replica scaling, guardrails, and automated evaluation infrastructure. Outcomes & KPIs Key Outcome(s) Owned: Sub-hundred-millisecond SLM and detection service execution speeds across high-volume tenant workloads. Highly resilient, auto-scaling GPU inference cluster infrastructure with automated CI/CD and regression gating. Success Metrics / KPIs : P95 and P99 detection latency for prompt injection (PI) and classification services. GPU pod readiness time and cluster auto-scaling efficiency under burst traffic. Service availability and rate-limiting guardrail enforcement per tenant. Automated MLOps/LLMops pipeline throughput and deployment turnaround time. What You'll Do Architect, build, and optimize production serving pipelines for Small Language Models (SLMs) and traditional ML models using model quantization, batching, and GPU acceleration. Own and scale backend microservices (e.g., sds-service-prompt-injection, sds-service-ddr) delivering real-time threat detection. Build consumption-based monitoring, tenant rate-limiting, and runtime guardrail infrastructure. Manage and optimize GPU cluster replicas (Kubernetes / Pod infrastructure) to minimize cold-start times and manage infrastructure costs. Build continuous evaluation, automated retraining pipelines, model CI/CD, and automated regression gates to test model detection quality against live benchmarks. Refactor legacy service boundaries, service-to-service auth flows, and backend database configurations. Requirements: 5+ years of software engineering experience building distributed backend systems or high-throughput microservices. Proven track record in model serving and inference optimization (e.g., TensorRT, vLLM, ONNX Runtime, Triton Inference Server). Strong programming experience in Python, Go, or C++. Hands-on expertise with Kubernetes, container orchestration, GPU scheduling, and infrastructure auto-scaling. Solid understanding of CI/CD pipelines, MLOps/LLMops principles, and cloud infrastructure (AWS/GCP). Preferred / Nice to Have : Experience building consumption-based rate limiting or multi-tenant guardrail architectures. Familiarity with database refactoring, auth protocols, and backend technical debt remediation. Background in cybersecurity, threat detection engines, or DLP/PII filtering platforms. Experience benchmarking runtime vs. accuracy trade-offs between local SLMs and cloud LLMs (e.g., Vertex AI). Experience with AWS, GCP, Terraform, Kubernetes, and Linux. Follow us on LinkedIn ! title: Security Engineer - Detection and Response

Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team. Understanding of the German connection landscape: Working knowledge of the TSO/DSO hierarchy, the connection/integration process, and the technical connection rules (such as VDE-AR-N 4110/4120) a grid-connected asset must meet before it can participate in the energy markets. Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution. Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation. CAD, diagrams and tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion. Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with a team that is partly based in another country. Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them. Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration. A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time. Location and travel: Ideally based close to Kraken’s Berlin office . Willingness to travel to customers and sites in Germany, and occasionally to our Manchester team, although travel is kept to a minimum. title: Forward Software Engineer, Data
description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. About The Job As a Forward Software Engineer, Data, you will build the systems behind some of the hardest problems Mistral takes on. You join our team of engineers in Applied AI. We gravitate towards hard problems, decide how to solve them, and ship fast. You work closely with our customer-facing teams, and what works goes into production with our customers and across the company. When a project needs it, you work directly on customer engagements. We're looking for a strong software engineer who builds end to end and has shipped ML or GenAI systems to production. You've felt the pain of models that pass every eval and fail on real data, and of quality that drifts after launch. You've also felt the data engineering pain: pipelines that break silently, schemas that change under you, and backfills that take a weekend. Data engineering is your edge. You turn messy, large-scale data into systems that hold up. You think like a founder. You start from the customer's problem, not the technology. You measure success by the value you deliver, and you care about building experiences people love to use. You like working at the edge of what AI can do today, and you push past it. Your scope is end to end, from first prototype to production. Your depth in data architecture helps set the standard for how the team designs and delivers systems. You know lakehouse and data mesh patterns well enough to know when they fit and when they're overkill. You've designed ontologies and data models, and you know that getting them right is as much art as science. What you will do Build AI systems end to end, from first prototype to production. Design the data architecture underneath them: ingestion, processing, storage, and the data models and ontologies that make messy data usable. Build distributed pipelines that process large volumes of documents, code, logs, and multimodal content for retrieval, agentic workflows, and fine-tuning. Turn what works for one customer into patterns and platforms that work across many, without rebuilding each time. Make systems hold up under real load: throughput, latency, cost, and failure recovery are part of the design from the start. Build data governance into the systems themselves: ownership, access control, lineage, retention, and privacy for sensitive enterprise data. Build the evaluation loop: labeling with LLMs and humans, versioned eval datasets, and checks that catch quality drift before customers do. Set the standard for how the team designs and ships data systems. Work with researchers, engineers, and customer-facing teams to turn hard problems into systems people rely on. What We're Looking For You have full ability to ship across the stack: proficient NodeJS e.g. NextJS/Express/Fastify or similar or Python e.g. FastAPI. You are confident with TypeScript + React/NextJS or similar. Solid beats polished. You have 5+ years of experience building and running production data-intensive pipelines with distributed processing (for example Spark, Ray, Beam, or Dask) and orchestration tools (for example Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect) with structured and unstructured data. You have experience with retrieval-augmented generation, agentic use cases, or LLM evaluation, and a clear view of how data quality drives model quality. You work autonomously: you find the problem, decide the approach, and own the outcome. You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences, and are fluent in English. You ship in increments, are obsessed with time to value and are comfortable making and articulating product-technical tradeoffs. Ideally you have A passion for graph-based systems (e.g. Neo4j) and ontology design Hands-on experience building data pipelines for LLM training, fine-tuning, or evaluation, and contributions to open-source projects, particularly in data or LLMs. Hands-on experience with data governance and privacy requirements (for example GDPR), secure data handling, CI/CD and infrastructure as code, or an affinity for security engineering. How We Work in Applied AI We care about people and outputs. What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week. Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care. No politics. Low ego, high standards. We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it. What We Offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page . Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us. description: <h3>About the Position</h3> <p>We are looking for an experienced Network Engineer to join our Network Security team to help us to run, scale and continuously improve our network security infrastructure through hands-on operations, design, and implementation. The ideal candidate would have strong networking fundamentals and experience with security appliances such as firewalls and proxy to join our Network Security team.</p> <p>Jane Street’s numerous distributed systems are built on an agile, reliable, multi-vendor network infrastructure that supports all traffic profiles, from trading to internet connectivity. Supporting such a large multi-function network requires advanced tooling for monitoring and automation.&nbsp;</p> <p>Strong communication and interpersonal skills will be needed to collaborate with colleagues across the firm globally. You will find and resolve issues, plan and execute deployments, and improve systems where possible. In this role, we’ll look to leverage your advanced networking skills and security knowledge to:&nbsp;</p> <ul> <li>Work closely with Network Engineering on design and deployment of security perimeter and adjacent network infrastructure</li> <li>Effectively manage and continuously evolve network segmentation, DMZ, and other aspects of network security</li> <li>Evaluate and lab test new platforms for our network security infrastructure</li> <li>Collaborate with Cybersecurity on detection and mitigation of threats and vulnerabilities on our network</li> <li>Interface with application owners and traders to enable business workflows in a secure way</li> <li>Proactively enhance support by improving network infrastructure observability, scripting, and communicating requirements to our software engineers</li> <li>Improve our network security processes and documentation</li> </ul> <p>A holistic approach to system design is critical for this role. The Networking department prioritizes flexibility, compatibility, and efficiency when crafting solutions, all while seeking ongoing buy-in and feedback from users across the firm. Our firm’s culture prizes intellectual humility, openness, and continuous improvement, which translates directly to the daily work of this team. We’re all partners working towards shared goals and are always looking for the next best idea that will make our work stronger.&nbsp;</p> <p>Your strong communication skills and analytical thinking will be invaluable as we support the daily work of our colleagues and keep our systems operating at the highest standard.</p> <h3>About You</h3> <ul> <li>7+ years of experience operating and deploying network infrastructure</li> <li>Experience with routing and network protocols (OSPF, BGP, PIM-SM)</li> <li>Experience troubleshooting transport protocols (TCP/UDP)</li> <li>Strong understanding of firewall hardware architecture, performance metrics, and its functional components</li> <li>Experience with firewall configuration and troubleshooting</li> <li>Understanding of Public Key Infrastructure and related technologies</li> <li>Understanding of modern encryption techniques</li> <li>High capacity to learn; we are interested in how you think, not just what you know</li> <li>Ability to context switch, while still being able to prioritize and organize your stack&nbsp;</li> <li>Ideally experience with overlay networks (EVPN, VxLAN)</li> <li>A flexible and reliable team player who enjoys working in a collaborative environment</li> <li>Proficiency in a programming language is preferred but not required</li> <li>Fluency in English is required</li> </ul> <p><em>If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out ----- Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Graduate Analyst Programme - Capabilities
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142); font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;">About Baringa&nbsp;</span></h3> <p>Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.</p> <p>The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.</p> <p>Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.</p> <p>Certified as a&nbsp;<em>Great Place to Work </em>around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the <em>Financial Times </em>in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by <em>Forbes </em>for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.</p></div><h3><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">Our Graduate Analyst Programme</span></span></h3> <p>Our Graduate Analyst role offers the opportunity to start and grow your career at Baringa. As a permanent member of our team from day one, you'll work on a variety of real client and internal projects, develop valuable skills, and make a meaningful contribution from the outset.</p> <p>You'll work alongside experienced consultants, building both your technical and professional capabilities through structured learning, hands-on experience, and ongoing development opportunities. Along the way, you'll build relationships across the business, collaborate with colleagues from different teams and sectors, and contribute to work that makes a real impact.</p> <p>If you're a recent graduate looking to kick-start your career, Baringa offers a supportive and collaborative environment where you can develop your skills, gain practical experience, and build a successful long-term future with us.</p> <p>We're looking for <strong>Graduate Analysts</strong> to join our <strong>Capabilities</strong> practice, with opportunities available across several of our specialist business units. During the application process, you'll have the opportunity to select the business unit that best aligns with your interests and aspirations.</p> <p><strong>The business units currently hiring are:</strong></p> <p><strong>Customer</strong></p> <p>Imagine a world where customers are delighted, employee engagement soars and costs drop. This is the power of world-class omni-channel experiences. Our expert team anticipates change, crafting innovative solutions that blend seamlessly across all touchpoints. By leveraging cutting-edge technology, we transform service delivery, minimising costs while maximising impact. Ready to enhance your market position and unlock unprecedented value? Let’s redefine excellence together.</p> <p><em>Desired Skills: Strong communication, teamwork, and relationship-building skills. Structured problem-solving and analytical thinking. A customer-focused mindset and interest in improving customer experiences. AI and digital literacy with a curiosity for emerging technologies. Adaptability, curiosity, and a proactive approach to learning and development.</em></p> <p><em>Desired Degrees: Business Management, Product Design UX &amp; UI, and Marketing</em></p> <p><strong>Enterprise Value Creation</strong></p> <p>Every organisation faces moments when it needs to grow faster, operate more efficiently or respond to changing market conditions. Baringa's Enterprise Value Creation team helps clients navigate these challenges by combining strategic thinking, analytical rigour, AI-native mindset, and practical delivery expertise. We advise executive leadership teams to identify opportunities, solve complex business problems and deliver sustainable improvements in growth, profitability, and performance.</p> <p><em>Desired Skills: Structured problem solving, Data analysis, Digital and AI literacy, Team collaboration and personal communication, Adaptability, Commercial and financial curiosity.</em></p> <p><em>Desired Degrees: Open to all degree types.</em></p> <p><strong>Organisation, People &amp; Change </strong></p> <p>Organisation, People, and Change (OPC) enables organisations to achieve lasting success by putting people at the centre of transformation. With a holistic approach, our team helps clients align their operating models, people strategies, structures, and cultures with their strategic ambitions. OPC ensures organisations are equipped to deliver impact that lasts through an engaged and high-performing workforce.</p> <p>As part of OPC, you will have the opportunity to work across a range of sectors, helping clients with a range of solutions:</p> <ul> <li>Optimising operations and organisational design: Align business capabilities, processes, and technology with the strategic ambition to drive efficiency and effectiveness.</li> <li>Unlocking leadership, culture, and workforce potential: Shape future skills, foster an engaged and high-performing workforce, and embed target cultures through people-led experiences.</li> <li>Crafting and delivering transformation and change strategies: Define the vision, strategic direction, and OKRs to create positive conditions for change, enabling organisations to deliver lasting impact.</li> </ul> <p><em>Desired Skills: Excellent communication and collaboration skills, Strong critical thinking and problem-solving abilities, Organisation and project management capability, Curiosity, adaptability, and a growth mindset, AI literacy and an interest in innovation, A genuine passion for consulting and transforming organisations and workforces through meaningful change.</em></p> <p><em>Desired Degrees (not essential): Business management / Management and Organisational Behaviour, Psychology / Organisational Psychology, Engineering - critical thinking / problem solving, Data Analytics / Business Analytics.</em></p> <p><strong>Supply Chain &amp; Procurement </strong></p> <p>The SCP team helps organisations tackle complex challenges across their supply chains, procurement functions and commercial operations. Working with clients across the public and private sectors, we help organisations navigate an increasingly uncertain world, responding to challenges such as cost pressures, supply chain disruption, changing customer expectations and rapid technological change.</p> <p>As part of SCP, you'll work on a diverse range of projects spanning supply chain strategy, procurement transformation, commercial advisory, logistics, and technology-enabled change, as part of either our Supply Chain or Procurement &amp; Commercial practice. Our teams combine analytical thinking, practical problem-solving and deep industry expertise to help clients create efficient, resilient and sustainable organisations that deliver lasting value.</p> <p><em>Desired Skills: Structured problem solving, Team collaboration and effective communication, Adaptability and personal resilience, Proactive curiosity, Digital literacy.</em></p> <p><em>Desired Degrees: No degree preference, analytical capabilities are key. If you have commercial acumen this is a bonus. Candidates may benefit from STEM experience, but this is not a requirement.</em></p> <p><strong>Data, AI, Solutions &amp; Engineering</strong></p> <p>Expertly applied, data and AI empower you to operate smarter, innovate faster and compete harder. Blending exceptional technical skills with deep industry knowledge, our consultants make the possibilities real. We are experts in crafting practical data and AI solutions and integrating these into existing production workflows. Where data and AI requires new scalable technology, we work with you to establish the case for investment. And when new data insights are revealed, we ensure you have the right talent to unlock full value. Whether you are looking to establish a robust data infrastructure, foster a data-driven culture or ensure data and information security and compliance are maintained, we can help.</p> <p><em>Desired Skills: Problem Solving, Data Analysis, Data Literacy, Technical Data Skills - BI, Python, Engineering, ML, Other coding languages.</em></p> <p><em>Desired Degrees: STEM, Computer Science, Data Science, Other technical data/AI degrees</em></p> <h3><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">So, what's in it for you?</span></span></h3> <ul> <li>You’ll join with a cohort of our Graduate Analysts. title: AI Transformation Owner, CRO
description: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role The AI Transformation Owner drives the end-to-end AI agenda for the field organization, translating emerging AI capabilities into concrete enablement roadmaps, field use cases, and org-level strategy. You will partner closely with product and engineering teams to pilot and scale AI solutions, own the operational transformation plan needed to embed AI into day-to-day field workflows, and establish the governance framework that keeps AI adoption safe, compliant, and aligned with company standards. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move from strategy to execution without heavy oversight. This role reports to the Vice President, Enablement & AI. What You’ll Do AI Enablement Roadmap: Own and continuously evolve the roadmap for AI-driven enablement initiatives, prioritizing based on field impact, feasibility, and alignment with broader Enterprise AI team and strategy.. AI Field Use Cases: Identify, scope, and execute on high-value AI use cases for the field (e.g., deal support, prospecting, content generation, guided selling, skills, change management), working with stakeholders to define success criteria and measure impact. AI Field Champions: build relationships with champions in the field organization to activate power-usage and drive peer-led adoption; track this adoption (e.g., usage, proficiency, behavior change) with our AI Ops Specialist and Enablement Analyst. Ops Transformation Plan: Design and drive the operational plan that turns AI pilots into scaled, repeatable processes, coordinating across enablement, ops, and technical teams to remove execution bottlenecks. AI Governance: Influence and lead governance standards for AI tool adoption in the field, including data usage, risk review, tool vetting, and alignment with company-wide AI policy. What You’ll Bring Mid-Senior Experience: Several years of experience in enablement, sales operations, or a related GTM function, with a track record of owning initiatives end-to-end. AI Solutions Experience: Direct experience evaluating, piloting, or deploying AI tools or solutions in a business context, with a solid technical understanding of how they work and where they add value. Act as the field's primary advocate for AI tools (e.g., AI-assisted prospecting, call intelligence, forecasting copilots, RFP/proposal generation). Cross-Functional Fluency: Proven ability to work closely with product and engineering teams, translating field needs into technical requirements and vice versa. Self-Sufficiency: Comfortable operating with significant autonomy — able to define scope, structure ambiguous problems, and drive work forward without needing detailed direction. Organization & Execution: Strong project management instincts; able to manage multiple workstreams (roadmap, use cases, ops transformation, governance) in parallel without dropping details. title: Security Solutions Engineer
description: About Nebius : Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. The role We are seeking a Security Solutions Engineer with a strong background in strategic solution evaluation, vendor assessment, and hands-on Proof-of-Concept (PoC) validation. This role is a crucial bridge between identifying customer security requirements and implementing best-in-class, enterprise-grade solutions. You will be responsible for defining the criteria, researching the market, and executing technical validation for all major security tooling and services adopted by the company. Key responsibilities: 1. Strategic Research & Requirement Definition Threat-to-Solution Mapping: Proactively analyze customer expectations, regulatory/compliance drivers, and threat models to define precise functional and non-functional requirements for new security solutions. Market Analysis & Scouting: Conduct thorough market scans to identify cutting-edge security products, platforms, and vendors across key domains (e.g., CSPM/CNAPP, DLP, IAM/IGA, EDR/XDR, data security, Kubernetes security, and AI/ML security). Vendor Due Diligence: Evaluate potential vendors based on technical capability, security posture, integration requirements, roadmap, data residency/compliance, and support quality, and shortlist candidates for the PoC phase. 2. Technical Validation & Proof-of-Concept (PoC) Leadership PoC Planning & Design: Develop detailed, objective, and threat-aligned test plans and success criteria for all security solution Proof-of-Concepts (PoCs), including quantitative success metrics, coverage of key attack scenarios, and opportunities for automation. Hands-on Environment Setup: Independently architect and deploy isolated PoC environments that accurately simulate our production infrastructure (e.g., setting up cloud VPCs, Kubernetes clusters, integrating with test data via IaC, and mimicking typical workloads). Testing & Analysis: Execute security research methodologies within the PoC (e.g., simulating attack scenarios, conducting deep feature validation, assessing false positive/negative rates) to rigorously test the vendor solution's effectiveness. Artifact Generation: Document all findings, including technical performance data, integration challenges, security gaps discovered, and clear comparative analysis metrics. 3. Decision Support & Communication Recommendation & Insight: Deliver comprehensive, data-driven reports and compelling presentations to security and product leadership and engineering stakeholders, providing a clear recommendation for the optimal solution and vendor selection. Integration Planning: Work closely with Security Engineering, Platform/Infra, and DevOps teams to ensure selected solutions are feasible to integrate, operate, and scale, and to hand off PoC learnings into implementation plans. Must-haves: Experience: Minimum 6+ years in Security Engineering, Security Architecture, or a dedicated Security Research role focused on solution validation and vendor management. Technical Depth: Deep understanding of modern cloud security principles (e.g., AWS/Azure/GCP security models, Kubernetes/containers, network segmentation, IaC scanning, least privilege, identity-centric security, confidential computing). Programming and Automation - Strong scripting / programming skills (e.g., Python, Go, or similar) for automating PoCs, building test harnesses, and integrating tools via APIs and CI/CD pipelines. Solutions Expertise: Proven, hands-on experience with the architecture, deployment, and testing of two or more enterprise-grade security tools (e.g., SIEM/SOAR platforms, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Vulnerability Management, Secrets Management). PoC Proficiency: Demonstrated ability to plan and execute complex technical Proof-of-Concepts, including setting up test environments and defining quantitative success metrics. Soft Skills: Exceptional analytical skills with the ability to translate complex technical findings into clear business risk and strategic recommendations. Strong written and verbal communication. Experience in a compliance-focused industry (e.g., finance, healthcare, or cloud infrastructure) and familiarity with frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2, or GDPR. Advanced professional certifications such as CISSP, CCSK or relevant cloud certifications (e.g., AWS/GCP/Azure Security Specialty). Key Responsibilities Technical Pre-sales & Bid Management Analyze customer technical specifications, RFIs, RFQs, and RFPs for utility-scale solar, wind, and hybrid BESS assets. Author technical proposals, functional architecture diagrams, and Statements of Work (SOW) for EMS/SCADA solutions. Compile compliance matrices and deviation lists addressing customer specifications and utility regulations. Define the Bill of Materials (BOM), covering server hardware, industrial controllers, networking equipment, software licenses, and engineering services. Lead technical deep-dive workshops, solution demonstrations, and clarification sessions with customers, EPC contractors, and grid operators. Grid Code Compliance & Functional Control Design Evaluate regional Grid Code regulations across target European markets (e.g., VDE-AR-N 4110/4120, ENTSO-E standards) and translate them into EMS/PPC control requirements Architect plant-level control logic, including Active Power Control, Reactive Power/Power Factor Regulation, POI/PCC Voltage Support, Frequency Response, and Ramp Rate restrictions. Define EMS-level operational strategies, such as automated dispatch tracking, State of Charge (SoC) management constraints, energy arbitrage scheduling, ancillary service controls, and fail-safe/black-start logics. System Integration & Communication Architecture Design overall system architectures connecting EMS, PPC, SCADA, Historian, and Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI). Define interface specifications for external subsystems: Battery Management Systems (BMS), Power Conversion Systems (PCS), MV switchgear, digital protection relays, power meters, and TSO/DSO dispatch centers. Develop and maintain interface control documents (ICD), data point lists, and signal mapping registers. Implement and validate standard industrial protocols, including Modbus TCP/RTU, IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850 (MMS/GOOSE), DNP3, and OPC UA. Architect high-availability schemes, redundancy topologies, automated failover mechanisms, time synchronization (NTP/PTP), and disaster recovery plans. OT Networking & Cybersecurity Architecture Design Operational Technology (OT) network topologies, VLAN segmentations, IP addressing schemes, and DMZ firewall policies. Formulate secure remote maintenance topologies, jump host concepts, VPN tunnels, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) mechanisms. Ensure EMS solution adherence to cybersecurity standards, including IEC 62443 and IEC 62351 frameworks. Collaborate with customer IT/OT security teams and external auditors during security reviews and threat modeling assessments. Verification & Handover Define verification scopes and technical criteria for Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), and grid compliance commissioning. Support engineering, commissioning, and project management teams during post-award handover to ensure seamless project delivery. Primary high/medium voltage electrical hardware engineering (transformers, switchgear internals, or EPC civil infrastructure). Professional Experience: 3 to 5+ years of experience in technical presales, solution architecture, or systems engineering focusing on EMS, PPC, or SCADA in power generation or grid utilities. Practical familiarity with grid integration procedures and technical dialogue with European grid operators (TSOs/DSOs). Technical & Protocol Competencies: Solid understanding of power utility communication standards: IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850, Modbus TCP/RTU, DNP3, and OPC UA . Hands-on experience with industrial automation platforms (PLCs/RTUs), real-time historians, and SCADA packages. Working knowledge of industrial cybersecurity best practices ( IEC 62443 / IEC 62351 ). Key Competencies: Strong analytical capability to dissect technical tender documents into structured requirements. Confident presentation skills in customer-facing technical exchanges and contract negotiations. Language Skills: Professional fluency in English (written and verbal) is required. Own Abby Care's AI governance program, the responsible AI policy suite, AI inventory, AI use case intake and review process, model risk classification, ongoing monitoring, and AI incident response, and evolve it as the regulatory and deployment landscape shifts. Own the AI use case review framework, risk tiering, and SLAs for internal generative and agentic AI tools and for AI-powered features in Abby Care's product, including chart update, documentation extraction, and clinical decision support. Exercise final legal sign-off and escalate enterprise-level risk decisions to the General Counsel. Set regulatory change management strategy across federal and state privacy, health data, and AI law. Translate horizon scanning into program and product decisions, not just memos. Lead privacy and AI incident response, including investigation, breach analysis, regulator and individual notification, and post-incident program remediation. Own the privacy and AI sections of the Board package and present privacy and AI risk to the Board of Directors or its designated committee. Manage outside privacy and AI counsel relationships, including scope, budget, and quality of work product. Hire, develop, and lead the privacy and AI team as it grows. Serve as Abby Care’s HIPAA Privacy Officer, and partner with the General Counsel and Compliance leadership on training and awareness programs, and the integration of privacy and AI controls into the broader compliance program. What success looks like: In your first six months, you have taken full operational ownership of the privacy and AI governance programs from the General Counsel. You have completed a program assessment, set the 12-month work plan, and aligned the GC and Compliance leadership on it. The AI use case review process is yours — documented, in operation, and meeting SLAs you set. The BAA program has a refreshed template, a clear playbook, and a current portfolio. In your first twelve months, Abby Care's privacy program is operating against documented standards that you own, with active monitoring, a current data map, a refreshed BAA portfolio, and a tested incident response workflow. The AI governance program is operating end-to-end and has reviewed every AI use case in production and in the active product pipeline. In year two, the privacy and AI programs are running on a predictable cadence, with measurable improvements year over year and meaningful leverage from the team growing under you. title: Test Engineer (all genders) - Remote Germany or Hungary
description: About Linro Linro is a Berlin-based cloud security company building a real-time, agentic cloud-security platform. Teams ship with AI. AI ships with Linro. Infrastructure changes constantly, and increasingly it's AI agents making the changes. Tools that scan snapshots and flag risk after the fact can't keep up. Linro enforces intended state across the whole lifecycle instead, from commit to runtime: MCP and pre-commit hooks at commit time, blast-radius simulation that blocks bad changes before they ship, and real-time detection, enforcement and auto-remediation in production. Most tools tell you what's wrong. Linro stops it. We have each been on the receiving end of this problem: Running cloud security at scale, building the platforms underneath it, and shipping in regulated systems where a wrong change isn't an option. Founded in Berlin in 2026 and built fully remote across Europe, Linro has a platform that's real and working, with plenty still to shape. The role You would be our dedicated quality engineer, working with the engineering team. Linro runs across many plugins and integrations, and at its core a policy engine decides whether a cloud change is compliant. If it decides wrong, a customer either ships a change that fails their audit or gets blocked for no good reason. You build and own the process that proves it all works: the test strategy, an automated regression suite for the core engine and every plugin and integration, and the quality gates between AI-written code and production. Automation first, manual testing where it makes more sense. What you will do Own the test strategy and the regression platform: nightly, pre-release and production runs against live installs, with reporting people trust and a clear line between environment noise and real regressions. We use Playwright today; the tooling is your call as long as it works and is easy to operate. Own the correctness of the policy engine: build a reference set of test cases with known expected results, plus property-based and differential tests, so policies evaluate the same way across past, present and simulated future state. Run the test environments: real sandbox cloud accounts, cloud emulators, capacity and cost per environment. Own the CI quality gates in GitHub Actions, and review the tests and changes our AI coding agents produce. Extend coverage across the web frontend (components and user flows), the plugins and integrations, the MCP server and the guardrails agents call, including basic security testing. What we are looking for 4+ years in test or quality engineering for distributed backend or cloud products. You write and review real code. We use Go and TypeScript, but any language works. You use AI coding agents daily and have a view on how tests become the control layer when agents write the code. Strong written, async communication and the judgement to call a failure a product bug, a test bug or environment noise. End-to-end testing, built and operated. You know how end-to-end tests really work across UI, APIs and the infrastructure underneath, and you have run them as pipelines yourself: nightly and pre-release runs against live environments, test data and environment setup, flaky-test handling and reporting that people trust. Playwright or similar tooling. API, integration and frontend testing: gRPC or ConnectRPC services and the databases behind them, plus component and UI tests for a TypeScript web frontend. A strategy for correctness-critical logic: golden files, property-based and differential testing, and a habit of asking what a false "compliant" would cost. Hands-on cloud, Terraform and Kubernetes with Helm, including ephemeral environments and keeping cloud cost in check. Nice to have Hands-on experience with Terraform, Kubernetes and Helm. Cloud control-plane or IAM knowledge, or a security testing background. Experience testing MCP servers or LLM-agent flows (non-deterministic evals). How we work We work remotely across Europe. We get the whole team together in person somewhere in Europe once a quarter for a few days. We work async by default, write things down, and protect people's focus time. Engineers here ship with AI agents every day, so review and tests carry more weight than in most teams. What we offer Real ownership. You are the first dedicated quality hire: you design the strategy, own the platform and have a say in how we build. Meaningful equity. You are an early employee, and your stake reflects it. Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market. A quarterly European offsite, and a team that takes both the mission and each other's time seriously. The honest version This is early. Our regression platform is real but still being rebuilt: some environments are noisy, some tests are parked, and some coverage does not exist yet. There is no test plan waiting for you to execute. If you want a mature QA organisation with a stable framework and a ticket queue, this is not it. If you want to build the quality system for a product whose whole promise is being right, and you like the idea of keeping AI-written code honest, we should talk. Your judgements are your own: you set the sample, raise and classify findings, and report outcomes on the evidence, without direction from the customer or from Baines Simmons. title: DACH Enterprise Account Executive – SAP Ecosystem & Digital Transformation (m/f/d)
description: DACH Enterprise Account Executive – SAP Ecosystem & Digital Transformation (m/f/d) Position Summary:  We are looking for an Enterprise Account Executive, reporting to the VP of Global GTM. We are seeking an elite, high-performing Enterprise Account Executive to drive new business acquisition across top-tier accounts. Combining large-enterprise sophistication with an aggressive, entrepreneurial hunting mindset, you will architect transformational security deals, engage C-level stakeholders, and position business resilience for the world's most mission-critical ERP environments.   Key Responsibilities Drive Strategic Revenue: Own the full sales lifecycle for Global 2000 accounts, positioning the Onapsis Platform as the essential security layer for SAP and Business Critical Applications.    The SAP "Triple Threat":   Direct Sales: Manage complex, high-value "land and expand" cycles. SAP Co-Sell: Partner with SAP Account Executives (AEs) and Enterprise Architects  to attach Onapsis to S/4HANA and RISE migrations. GSI Alignment: Orchestrate go-to-market strategies with Global Systems Integrators (Accenture, Deloitte, IBM, PwC) who are leading the world's largest SAP transformations.   C-Suite Advisory: Act as a trusted advisor to CISOs and CIOs, translating technical vulnerabilities into business risks (e.g., SOX compliance, financial downtime, and data integrity).   Territory Orchestration: Develop and execute an annual territory plan focused on "White Space" analysis within the SAP installed base.   Forecast Accuracy: Maintain a high level of "Sales Hygiene" within CRM, delivering predictable weekly and monthly forecasts aligned with SAP's rigorous reporting standards.   Required Skills/Experience:   Proven Enterprise Track Record: 7–10+ years of enterprise software sales experience, with a proven history of selling complex software solutions within the SAP ecosystem (either at SAP or a top-tier partner). Cloud Transformation Expert: Deep understanding of the RISE with SAP framework, Clean Core strategy, and the SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) . Consistent High Achiever: Consistent record of quota over-achievement, regularly closing seven-figure ARR deals across Global 2000 accounts with complex buying committees. Alliance Savvy: Demonstrated success in "partner-first" selling, particularly with GSIs and SAP's regional field teams. Communication: Exceptional executive presence; ability to move seamlessly from a technical discussion with a Basis Lead to a strategic ROI pitch with a CFO. Ability to travel: We believe that our business is a people business and that trust is built in person. Between 25-50% travel required.  Entrepreneurial Mindset: Proactive self-starter with the drive to build a territory from scratch and take full ownership of business growth.Languages: Professional fluency in both German and English (written and spoken). What You will get:  You can expect a job with responsible tasks and creative opportunities, an attractive salary and extensive benefits (including JobRad, Focus Friday and much more). You have flexible working hours with us. In addition, you can work remotely from other EU countries by arrangement. We support our employees with 5 fully paid sick days per child and subsidize childcare up to primary school age. In addition to an individual onboarding and buddy program, we offer comprehensive training opportunities and english language classes. We offer 30 days of paid vacation per year (based on a 5-day workweek) for optimal work-life balance. Furthermore, you can expect an innovative and attractive workplace with flat hierarchies and respectful and solution-oriented communication. Equity in a late-stage, high-growth leader backed by top-tier VC/PE firms. The chance to represent the only cybersecurity solution endorsed by SAP.   About Onapsis: Onapsis protects the business applications that run the global economy. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As an AI Transformation Owner at GitLab, you'll shape your function's AI strategy and build the solutions that deliver it. You are the person responsible for identifying where AI can fundamentally change how your org operates, partnering with your Executive Sponsor to align on the biggest challenges, and driving measurable outcomes against them. Think of this as a product management role where the product is your org's way of working. You'll manage the full lifecycle: understanding how work flows today, deciding where AI should reshape it, prioritizing what gets built and in what order, and ensuring what ships actually gets adopted. You'll also prototype solutions, configure agents, and prove what's possible before pulling in engineering support to scale it. You will work closely with an AI Engineer who sits within the Enterprise AI team. Together you form a partnership: you bring the business context, process intelligence, and strategic prioritization. They bring the technical depth, production-grade delivery, and architecture decisions. You'll build working solutions at the no-code and low-code layer, and partner with the AI Engineer on the right approach, tooling, and structure. What you'll do Strategy & Prioritization Own your function's AI strategy, aligned with your Executive Sponsor and business priorities. Understand which metrics matter to the org, identify what will move the needle, define how you'll measure impact, and track progress over time. Map how work flows across your function end-to-end, including the handoffs upstream and downstream to other orgs. Identify where the real constraints are, not just the ones your team can see. Focus on the 100x problems: where could leveraging AI in a workflow let your org execute it orders of magnitude faster, or at 100x more volume than before? Manage intake of AI requests, ideas, and pain points from across the function, including via your Champion network. Ensure every team member has a clear route to surface what they need, rather than building independently. Prioritize strategically against business outcomes and executive guidance. Hold the line on priorities - we cannot change direction every two weeks - and ensure the AI Engineer's time is spent on the highest-impact work. Adoption & Change Management Reimagine, not just automate. Challenge your org to think beyond injecting AI into existing workflows. Work with Enterprise AI to spot opportunities to fundamentally rethink how work gets done. Drive adoption and change management together with the AI Engineer. The best AI solution is worthless if nobody uses it. Create the channels, rituals, and feedback loops that make AI visible in your function: shared spaces for teams to show what they've built, regular office hours, onboarding for new hires, and celebration of wins. Own the rollout and iteration needed to make AI initiatives stick. Coordinate with Enterprise AI to ensure your function benefits from patterns, tools, and learnings emerging across other parts of the business. Build and bridge the Champion network in your function. Champions are the peer community that extends your reach beyond what you and the AI Engineer can deliver directly. From early in the role, identify and recruit Champions across sub-teams (5-10% time, formally agreed with their manager), run a regular Champion sync, host demos to the wider function, and act as their bridge to Enterprise AI. Champions are not your reports: you coordinate them, you don't manage them. Without this network, your reach is capped. Hands-On Building & Agent Operations Build AI agents using no-code and low-code platforms (e.g. Glean, Workato, similar tools). Go from idea to working prototype without waiting for engineering. Author and iterate on skills files that define how AI agents behave. Refine instructions based on real usage and share reusable skills across the function. Configure MCP servers and tools, giving agents access to the business systems they need. Partner with the AI Engineer on what to connect and how to do it securely. Own your function's fleet of agents. Some agents will be used directly by people in your org. Those that aren't, you own. Either way, you're accountable for their performance: tracking KPIs, running evaluations after model or data changes, and iterating based on what you learn. Expect to rebuild. AI tools and models evolve fast. The agent you built last month may need to be replaced, not patched. You should be comfortable sunsetting your own work when a better approach emerges, and helping your org stay current rather than attached to what exists today. What you'll bring Business & Strategic Deep knowledge of your function's operations. You understand how work moves through your org, where it gets stuck, and why. You can trace a process end-to-end and explain how it connects to the teams around it. Strategic prioritization skills. You've managed competing demands before and can make hard calls about what matters most. You think in terms of business outcomes, not activity. A product management mindset. You naturally think about intake, backlog, iteration, and adoption. You're comfortable defining success metrics and holding yourself accountable to them. Strong communication and influence. You'll be the person saying "not yet" to some teams and "think bigger" to others. You need the credibility and interpersonal skills to make both of those conversations land. Cross-functional instincts. You default to understanding how your org's processes affect and are affected by the teams around you - not just optimising in isolation. Experience building peer networks or communities of practice. You've recruited and sustained volunteer contributors before, whether as a guild lead, champion program owner, or community organizer. You know how to motivate people whose time you don't directly own. Hands-On & Technical Comfortable building with AI tools. You don't need to write production code, but you should be able to build a working agent, configure a skill, connect an MCP server, and troubleshoot when something isn't working. Think: power user, not software engineer. Ready to learn fast. Experience with or willingness to quickly pick up no-code/low-code AI platforms, prompt engineering, and agent configuration. You'll be trained on GitLab's specific tooling, but you should arrive ready to get your hands dirty. Strong conceptual understanding of AI capabilities - summarization, classification, generation, automation, agentic workflows - and a commitment to staying current. The landscape shifts constantly. The tools you use today may be obsolete in weeks. You stay on top of new developments so that your org's AI strategy reflects what's actually possible, not what was possible six months ago. Ability to map data flows - structured and unstructured. Understand where agents need context, and figure out where humans should interface with automated workflows and at what steps. About the team You will partner closely with Enterprise AI within the Enterprise Technology & AI organization, while remaining embedded in your own function. Enterprise AI provides the technical delivery capability, platforms, and patterns. You provide the business context, prioritization, building at the no-code layer, and adoption muscle. description: At Submittable , we are transforming how organizations create social impact. Our platform empowers thousands of mission-driven organizations, from nonprofits to government entities, to make a difference in their communities and beyond. In 2024, our innovative software helped organizations worldwide run 30,000 programs , welcomed 1.2 million applicants , and facilitated the distribution of more than $10 billion in funding through our products on behalf of our clients. We are on a mission to help organizations accelerate their impact, so we are proud to partner with organizations focused on Equity & Social Justice, Children & Education, Creative & Arts, Health & Wellness, Economic Justice & Opportunity, and Environment & Climate. At Submittable, technology and purpose converge, offering a unique opportunity to contribute to meaningful change. About the Role Submittable is hiring a Vice President of Engineering who is deeply technical, works hands-on, and builds with AI every day. You will report to the CTO and run engineering day to day: delivery, quality, reliability, cost, and the people who make them happen. We want a different VP than the old SaaS playbook produced. That playbook grew output by growing headcount and adding layers of management. We believe AI coding tools now let a small team of strong engineers ship what once took a team several times its size. We intend to run engineering that way. You will keep the organization lean, keep layers few, and raise output per engineer rather than the number of engineers. You cannot lead that change from a slide deck. You need to know firsthand what it is like to ship production software with AI agents, including where they fail. We expect you to have done this yourself in the last 12 months and to keep doing it here. Plan on roughly a fifth of your week going to hands-on technical work: reading and writing code, reviewing pull requests, working incidents, and building the tools your teams use. We are choosing depth over span. This is a hands-on leadership role for a small, senior team, not a role leading a large organization through layers of managers. If you want to make architecture calls, contribute and ship code, and help a lean team deliver well beyond its size, we want to talk. What You'll Do Run engineering day to day. Turn the CTO's technical strategy and the product roadmap into plans, priorities, and shipped software. Stay hands-on. Review pull requests, prototype, debug production issues, and write tools. You should be able to pick up a ticket and ship it. Teams should trust your calls because of your technical judgment, not your title. Make AI the default way we build. Expect every engineer to work with AI coding agents (tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot) for design, coding, testing, and review. Show people how by doing it yourself, and remove whatever stops them. Measure what AI changes. Track the four DORA metrics (how often we deploy, how long a change takes to reach production, how often changes fail, and how fast we recover), plus defects that reach customers and engineering cost per release. Report plainly on where AI helps and where it creates new problems, such as oversized pull requests, thinner review, or code no one on the team understands. Keep the organization lean. Grow output faster than headcount. Keep management layers thin, expect managers to stay technical, and favor small teams with clear ownership over large teams that need heavy coordination. Before adding a person, ask whether better tooling or automation solves the problem. Automate the toil. Use AI and automation for test generation, CI/CD checks, code review assistance, release notes, incident triage, and alerting, so engineers spend their time on the product. Raise the technical bar. Set standards for architecture, code review, testing, CI/CD, release management, and incident response. Shipping more code, faster, raises the stakes for review, testing, and observability. Make sure speed does not cost us quality. Own platform reliability, security, and cost. Our products are multi-tenant SaaS running on AWS and Azure, with Kubernetes. Work with infrastructure and security partners to meet uptime targets, pass SOC 2 audits, and keep cloud spend growing slower than revenue. Simplify our architecture where consolidation pays for itself. Build AI into the product. Work with the CTO and Product to add AI to Submittable so customers can set up programs, review applications, and make funding decisions in less time. Help decide what to build and how to test it for accuracy and fairness, because real applicants' outcomes depend on it. Hire and grow a small, strong team. Recruit engineers and leaders who already build with AI. Coach managers to stay close to the work. Build career paths that reward impact and technical depth, not team size. Partner across the company. Work with Product and Design on scope and trade-offs among new features, technical debt, and platform health. Work with Customer Experience and Support to resolve escalations and reduce customer-facing defects. What We're Looking For You have shipped software with AI in the last 12 months. You personally built and shipped production code using AI coding tools within the past year. You can tell us what you built, which tools you used, what broke, and how it changed the way you work. This is a requirement, not a preference. Deep technical skill. 15+ years in software engineering, with real depth in distributed systems, API design, data modeling, cloud infrastructure (AWS and Azure, Kubernetes), and DevOps. You can hold your own in an architecture review with our strongest engineers and spot the flaw in a design or a pull request. You have run lean, high-output teams. 7+ years in engineering leadership, including at least 3 years leading other managers. You have raised a team's output without matching growth in headcount, and you can show the numbers: delivery metrics, team size, and cost, before and after. B2B SaaS at scale. Experience building and running multi-tenant, cloud-based B2B SaaS products. Experience consolidating platforms or integrating acquired products is a plus. Predictable delivery. A record of shipping complex software on predictable timelines without trading away quality, security, or reliability. Distributed teams. You have led teams across multiple countries and time zones, including offshore or nearshore partners. You write clearly, because much of this work happens in writing. Comfort with fast change. The norms for building software now shift every few months. You form a view, test it, and change your mind when the evidence says so. A clear storyteller. You can explain technical trade-offs to executives and non-technical colleagues in plain language. You tell people where engineering is going and why, often enough that they repeat it. A builder of strong teams. A track record of hiring, developing, and keeping strong engineers and building inclusive teams. Nice to Have: Experience in a private equity-backed or high-growth SaaS company; familiarity with SOC 2 and GDPR; experience shipping LLM-based features to customers, including how to evaluate them. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Location: This is a remote, U.S.-based role — you must live and reside in the U.S. full-time. Salary Details: The annual salary range for this position is $220,000 - $260,000. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. We also have a location-based compensation structure; there may be a different range for candidates in other locations. We are interested in every qualified candidate eligible to work in the United States; however, we cannot accommodate scholastic or employment visas at this time . description: President & Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Aviation Information Sharing and Analysis Center (Aviation ISAC) Reports To: Board of Directors Location: Remote / Global FLSA Status: Exempt Travel: Up to 30% domestic and international travel Home Base : United States Position Summary The President & Chief Executive Officer (CEO) serves as the senior executive leader of the Aviation Information Sharing and Analysis Center (Aviation ISAC), a global nonprofit organization dedicated to reducing cyber risk and strengthening resilience across the aviation sector. The organization’s membership comprises 155 members across 41 countries, spanning five continents, demonstrating its extensive global reach and international representation. The CEO establishes the culture and provides strategic leadership and operational oversight to advance the organization's mission, vision, and long-term sustainability. The CEO serves as the primary liaison to the Board of Directors, member organizations, government agencies, industry associations, regulators, and strategic partners. The CEO is responsible for fostering a trusted global community that enables information sharing, knowledge development, stewardship, and partnership across the aviation ecosystem. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Aviation ISAC Core Values The President & CEO is expected to model and champion Aviation ISAC's five core values in all activities and decisions: Trusted Community Information Sharing Knowledge Development Stewardship Partnership The CEO is responsible for ensuring these values remain embedded within Aviation ISAC's culture, strategy, operations and execution. Strategic Leadership Lead the development and execution of Aviation ISAC's strategic plan. Identify and manage emerging opportunities, risks, and trends affecting aviation cybersecurity. Ensure the organization remains the leading trusted authority for global collaboration on aviation cybersecurity. Drive innovation in information sharing, threat intelligence, automation, community engagement, and member services. Seek advice and guidance on strategic priorities and organizational direction from the Board of Directors. Governance and Board Relations Serve as the principal advisor to the Board of Directors. Support the Board, Executive Committee, and standing committees through effective communication and reporting. Implement Board-approved policies, strategies, and resolutions. Ensure adherence to corporate governance requirements, bylaws, and fiduciary responsibilities. Maintain organizational compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and nonprofit requirements. Mission and Industry Leadership Act as the public face and chief spokesperson for Aviation ISAC. Represent the organization before industry groups, conferences, government agencies, regulators, and international bodies. Strengthen Aviation ISAC's role as a trusted voice on aviation cybersecurity and resilience. Promote collaboration among airlines, airports, OEMs, manufacturers, government agencies, and service providers. Advance Aviation ISAC's influence within the global aviation ecosystem. Membership Growth and Community Engagement Maintain and strengthen Aviation ISAC's trusted community. Establish membership growth and retention strategies. Ensure members receive exceptional value through intelligence products, communities of interest, training, events, and engagement opportunities. Foster collaboration among diverse member segments across the global aviation ecosystem. Financial Management and Stewardship Ability to oversee and manage an annual operating budget of approximately $6 million. Develop and oversee organizational budgets, forecasts, cash and investments, and financial planning. Must have financial and business acumen, with demonstrated ability to manage budgets, ensure organizational sustainability, prioritize investments, and align resources to strategic outcomes. Ensure responsible stewardship of organizational assets and resources. Monitor financial performance and organizational sustainability. Work with the Treasurer, Audit & Risk Committee, and Board to ensure sound financial governance. Identify and develop sponsorship, partnership, grant, and revenue opportunities consistent with the mission. Organizational Leadership Provide direct oversight and strategic direction for five key leadership roles: VP Member Success/CISO, VP Global Intelligence, VP Marketing/Event/Sponsors, Office Manager, and Business Development Manager, supporting a organizational workforce of 20 employees. Lead, develop, and inspire a high-performing remote workforce. Establish annual goals and performance expectations for senior leaders. Foster a culture of trust, accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement. Ensure organizational practices align with Aviation ISAC's Core Values and Vision. Promote employee development, succession planning, and organizational resilience. Information Security and Risk Management Ensure effective governance of information security, privacy, and risk management programs. Oversee implementation and maintenance of the Information Security Management System (ISMS). Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of member information and trusted sharing environments. Champion organizational resilience and business continuity planning. Partnerships and External Relations Develop and maintain strategic relationships with: Aviation industry stakeholders Government agencies Regulators Sector coordinating councils Research institutions Strategic technology and cybersecurity partners Pursue opportunities that enhance value to members and advance Aviation ISAC's mission. Facilitate collaboration on aviation cybersecurity issues of global significance. Leadership Competencies Strategic Vision Executive Leadership Board Governance Cybersecurity and Risk Awareness Member and Stakeholder Engagement Financial Acumen Relationship Building Public Speaking and Advocacy Organizational Development Change Leadership Consensus Building Ethical Decision-Making Preferred Qualifications Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred. Minimum 15 years of progressive leadership experience. U.S.-based residency required. Ability to obtain a U.S. government national security clearance highly desirable. Experience leading nonprofit, association, membership-based, aviation, cybersecurity, intelligence, or critical infrastructure organizations preferred. Familiarity with aviation industry stakeholders, cybersecurity risk management, information sharing communities, and regulatory environments. Demonstrated success working with Boards of Directors and senior executives. Proven ability to build partnerships and influence diverse stakeholders globally. Strong financial management and strategic planning experience. Exceptional communication and public speaking skills. title: Commercial Account Executive, UK
description: Get to Know Us Horizon3.ai is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organisations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. NodeZero has been adopted by organisations of all sizes, from small educational institutions to government agencies and Global 100 enterprises. It is used by ITOps/SecOps teams, consulting pentesters, and MSSPs and MSPs. We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results. Role Description Help shape the next stage of Horizon3.ai’s UK growth. Based in the Netherlands with regular UK travel, you’ll bring autonomous pentesting to new customers and help them reduce real-world security risk. If you thrive on opening doors, building partnerships and turning opportunities into wins, this is a chance to make a visible impact as we expand our UK Commercial team. We currently require our Amsterdam team to come to the office 2 - 3 days per week. What You’ll Do Grow Horizon3.ai’s UK Commercial business by winning new customers, developing productive channel partnerships and helping organisations realise value from our cybersecurity solutions. Win new accounts and expand our customer base by introducing disruptive cybersecurity software solutions to the UK market. Build and convert a qualified pipeline, owning the sales cycle from qualification and proof of value through negotiation and close, with the goal of exceeding quota consistently quarter over quarter. Turn channel partnerships into revenue by proactively engaging regional resellers and developing joint opportunities. Demonstrate Horizon3.ai solutions in virtual and in-person meetings, connecting technical capabilities to customer needs and business outcomes. Drive the post-proof of value ROI process, helping customers understand business value while building relationships that support satisfaction and retention. Maintain accurate customer records, pipeline data and forecasts in Salesforce so opportunities, risks and next steps are clearly understood. Work independently to progress opportunities while collaborating with distributed sales, support and customer success teams to deliver a coordinated customer experience. What You’ll Bring At least 5 years of successful cybersecurity sales experience, with a track record of driving growth, introducing disruptive software solutions and consistently exceeding quarterly quotas. Previous experience selling technical solutions into the UK market. Experience establishing and monetising channel partnerships; existing relationships with key regional resellers are essential. Proficiency across the full sales process, including qualification, proof of value, forecasting, negotiation, deal closure and post-proof of value ROI management. The ability to present and demonstrate cybersecurity solutions effectively, both virtually and in person. Strong CRM discipline and experience maintaining accurate pipeline records and forecasts in Salesforce (SFDC). Familiarity with Challenger Question-Based Selling-type methodologies and sales tools such as Outreach , LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo and Slack. The ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with distributed teams. Fluency in English; additional language skills are welcomed. Travel Required We are a hybrid company, and this job will require you to spend 3 days based at our Amsterdam city centre sales hub. The role may require up to 40% of travel within the assigned territory to be successful. Job-related travel expenses are reviewed and must be approved by your manager.
